title: Pretty Good Product!
text:
I bought 4 of these for my face painting business. We were going to be set up at a July 4th event, out in the middle of a field (no electricity), and I wasn't sure if we'd keep working after dark. I was pleasantly surprised by how well they worked. They weren't as bright as I was led to believe by other reviews, but we certainly could see well enough to continue working.

I'd hung two over each of us in the pop-up tent's roof supports - the lights come with handy fold out hooks. Again, it wasn't super bright, more of a grey/blue light, but it sure kept us working. The fans were nice, but they had to be set up right next to us on the table, set on high, to even notice anything. But, it was a VERY hot day and evening, 90-100. They were pretty quiet, just a hum.

I was torn, but didn't give it 5 stars because they are a little twitchy. Being made of lightweight plastic, you have to be careful of the switches, the slightest bump turns things on and off. Once set in place, they were fine. Also, I think parts could break easily with rough handling. But, for the price, what can you expect?

I am happy with the purchase, recommend them, and will use them again, happily. As long as you understand they aren't like electric lights, or super sturdy. But for the price, it's a great tent or camping light - they work pretty well.

title: Straightforward in an unspectacular way
text:
Since Mark Waid introduced a group of lab assistants to work under Bruce Banner, I’ve harped on the fact that they’ve had very little in the way of character development. The Indestructible Hulk #16 finally addresses that issue by delving into the past of Mr. Jessup, largely because, as this issue informs us, he’s going to die within a week. Spending a full issue to build up a character just so readers will feel some sort of impact when he dies seems a little cheap to me, but I still think this marks progress, as one of the things this book has been lacking is a good supporting cast.

The art here is done by Mahmud Asrar, who does a pretty good job. Nothing here really blows me away, but it’s a welcome change to have an entire issue follow one art style after the last arc cycled through multiple artists on a page-by-page basis.

As a whole, this issue does what it needs to do in a straightforward if unspectacular way. We finally get some background on some of Banner’s supporting cast, we get the suspense of knowing that said character is going to die, and we get some Hulk smashing action. This is an above-average issue that will hopefully lead into bigger things to come when the story gets rolling.

If you don't want a loud, tactile keyboard, don't buy a keyboard that is intentionally loud and tactile (no this cannot easily be changed after purchase) . But I LOVE how loud it is! :) And it does give a fantastic snappy feeling. Its my first mechanical keyboard... there are some obvious signs that it isn't a $200 + keyboard, likely because it doesn't cost $200+. It has an aluminum body which is great, but also allows a slightly hollow sounding release. The lighting isn't RGB, or programmable, and not 100% consistent across all keys (though it is like 98%, so it doesn't bother me and I don't even notice unless I'm looking to be critical). Its fantastic for gaming, I also use it for work sometimes, though as I type quite a lot for work, I've actually had to opt for a more ergonomic focused keyboard (a split design, good contours, etc), at no fault of this keyboard. I read a review saying it doesn't come with a wrist rest... of course not, it doesn't say it does. Most don't. But good wrist rests are affordable and easy to find - I prefer the freedom to choose my own anyways ;P. If you plan on using it around anyone, make sure they are ok with a very loud keyboard, it can be distracting.

text:
I first got this book from the library. I can honestly say, it wasn't what I was looking for at the time. As a new home brewer, I wanted to brew and drink drinkable beers as soon as I could. I have yet to meet a home brewer who has the necessary patience to make truly great brews right out of the gate. Not to say they aren't completely drinkable, just really following someone else's lead.

Half a year later I gave this book a second shot after reading "Brew Like a Monk". Reading it a second time was like two different books! What had happened?!? Well, obviously the book hadn't changed. My outlook on brewing had. It had matured and I had moved to a level of wanting to produce not only original, but consistent and delicious brews.

My first go-around I was essentially looking for shortcuts and recipes, therefore I was disappointed.

My second go-around I was really looking to understand what I was doing and wanting to control the process instead of just following a bunch of steps.

If all you want from home brewing is to brew good drinkable beer, save your money and put it towards ingredients or supplies. If you want to move your brewing and understanding of brewing to the next level in a very readable form, this book will be a good investment.

My copy of this cookbook has notes, and drips, and is yellowed and stained. It falls open on the gingersnap recipe because the spine is broken in that spot.  This simple cookie recipe has become full of memories for my husband, children and their friends as well. Other recipes in this little book look just as bad. It's been borrowed, copied, coloured in by a naughtly two year old [who is now a handsome young man] and is so dear to my heart that I could not bear to part with it in favor of a newer copy. It has, like the Velveteen Rabbit, become real. I would like to paint her rules of deportment on my breakfast room wall.

title: Alternative history strategy with a dash of random dice rolling
text:
As others have mentioned, Dust is like a beefed-up version of Risk where you can drop Mechanized Armor Units from the sky and send strategic bombers on a grand tour of alternate history WWII. It's fun, it's easy, and it requires just enough imagination and skill to keep you interested for hours.

The game itself comes with 2 rule books and about a million game pieces. The good news is, these pieces are actually kind of fun and more often than not you'll find yourself organizing units together as your opponent figures out his next move. Dust also comes with two different rule books, one for Premium and one for Epic. This is just shorthand for "long game" and "longer game". Along with these items, players also use cards to determine what types of moves they'll make and what special abilities they'll be able to bring into play with each turn.

If I only had one complaint with the game it's that it doesn't really capitalize on its theme all that much. Sure you get a great map of the apocalyptic future-scape, a ton of pieces representing everything from submarines to Mechs, and a card system that provides some pretty great artwork, but overall the whole idea of this "alternative history" World War II is all in your head. You don't really follow any stories, so most games end up being a large-scale RISK that doesn't suck as much as its predecessor.

All in all, I recommend this game for nothing else than being fun and entertaining.

title: User-Friendly Design, But Tricky Connection
text:
The BEST feature here is the dedicated buttons for each function, as opposed to the “rocker” style most of these remotes have. Also, these buttons are silent (unlike some of the others which sound like clickers!)

Unfortunately, this unit has one thing to BEWARE of. While the Manual directions are very clear about how to pair the Movo with your phone or other device, you get NO INSTRUCTIONS WHATSOEVER regarding connection/regular usage! This is unfortunate since making a Bluetooth connection is QUITE TRICKY.

HERE IS HOW TO CONNECT THIS REMOTE TO USE IT (this assumes you have already paired it up with your phone as per the directions): 1. Don’t even bother to open Settings; 2. Simply hold down the red Power button—BUT KEEP HOLDING IT DOWN until it turns first RED, then it FLASHES GREEN, then it becomes SOLID GREEN, then finally turns RED again. 3. RELEASE the Power button just as the light turns RED again!

This is the ONLY WAY I have found that works every time, and it is fairly easy. FAIRLY easy! Practice it a couple of times if you are having trouble with the connection.

Also, be sure to TURN THE POWER OFF when you’re finished using the Movo by holding the Power button down awhile—until the light turns red and then goes out! This will save battery life.

Once you get the hang of using the Power button, I think you will find this remote is a good one.

title: Not Enthusiastic
text:
OK, first the things I liked about the Littlest Pet Shop. All the parts were easy to assemble with clear instructions. The front panel is hinged so that little hands could get into the shop. Three "littlest pets" were included with the set. (It irks me when these "branded" sets are sold without the action figures.)

Now, for the things I didn't like. Though the sides, front, and base are made of sturdy plastic, the back panel was very thin cardboard. I had four little girls ages 5 to 10 "helping" me assemble the set, although they did more playing than assembling. Before we had gotten all the Deco bits taken off the plastic frames, the back panel had popped out of the frame. To restore it properly, several pieces had to be taken apart. For a play set that retails for $40, seems to me that the back panel could have been made from plastic, too. The sales counter was also a problem. It came in two pieces: the top and the base. The only way I could get the counter top to stay fastened to the base was to attach it with double-sided tape.

The set contains 135 pieces. A few pieces are decals. There are maybe 20 larger pieces. However, the rest are very small plastic pieces, the kind that small pets and toddlers choke on. The kind that children leave all over the floor and you step on in the middle of the night on your way to the bathroom or refrigerator. The kind you're still digging out from beneath the car seat when the child graduates from high school. Enough said?

In spite of my lack of enthusiasm for the Littlest Pets Shop Style Set, the 4 girls loved it. They happily played with everything. They set up the shop, decorated the side walls, the dog house, and the pets with the Deco Bits. They let the monkey swing from the chandelier and gave the pets new names. They just had fun. On their way out the door, the two older girls were asking their mom if they could go to the store. No one had to asked why...

title: This small unobtrusive piece of equipment will change the way you "see" things.....
text:

I live in the outskirts of Miami-Dade county and I am about 45 miles from the conglomerate of transmission towers for most of the main broadcast networks (ABC, CBS, FOX, PBS, TELEMUNDO, UNIVISION, etc).

According the chart on the webpage at AntennaWeb.org, if I was 45 miles from the networks, while using the Winegard FlatWave Air Outdoor HDTV antenna, I would be receiving anywhere from 20-30 channels. Since I've about had it handing over $200 plus to the cable company just to watch "what else in on tv" , I was shocked to find out that all the tuners in the 4 tv's in my house are receiving 92 channels of crystal clear reception.

I am ever the skeptic, but this antenna changed my perspective. One word of advice. You must use the included amplifier. Without it, I was only getting 7-8 channels.

The impressive part is that the antenna is mounted in the attic of my 2-story home. No strong winds, hurricanes or excessive rain to worry about.

Thank you Winegard and Amazon for helping me put more money in my savings account. Cable company......sucks being you !!!

title: I want more Lily Wong
text:
Lily Wong in The Ninja Betrayed transports us to a fantasy world that I would love to return to. Lily Wong is half Hong Kong Chinese but lives in the US. She agrees to accompany her mother to Hong Kong for a critical board meeting in her grandfather's company. We appreciate the subtle hints and language that the family and the business allies signal when Lily and her mother meet with the main shareholders. Lily soon realizes that the fight is more serious than expected and her mother's board seat is at risk.

The difference between what is said and what is meant is beautifully done. The scenes of the privileged life on Victoria Peak and the affluent areas of Hong Kong contrast with the intense protests against Mainland China's control over the island. Regardless of what Lily faces, she is a heroine in control of her environment, unafraid of physical risk, willing to face an overwhelming force, and quick to act. As we learn more about her history and demons, Lily Wong is someone that I want to spend time with.

title: Not for everyone, but provides unique principles to filter through the "noise"
text:
In today's work ecosystem of forced multitasking, being "busy" all the time, and never feeling comfortable saying "no", Essentialism provides unique principles for sorting through the noise and figuring out what is truly "essential". The author himself says brilliantly that "essentialism is not one more thing -- it's a whole new way of doing everything". The key principles that I have uncovered from this book are the following:
(1) Work effectively, not efficiently (the latter does not imply that you are working on THE most important things)
(2) Learn to say no to things (personal, work, etc) and take greater control of your life
(3) Actively funnel to-do's, requests, etc through an internal "essential" test to decide whether something is truely important and should be done at all

One caveat, similar to many books in this genre. If you are a low-ranking associate at your job, you will find it difficult to implement a fair number of these strategies Day 1 (e.g. "how the hell am I supposed to do this while working at a [law firm / bank / advertising agency / etc]). That being said, the principles are still worth reading and keeping with you, because as you grow more senior in your role (even if you're just managing one person initially), they will become incrementally more valuable

title: Recommend This Switch Box
text:
After several month's use on my HD flat panel TV, I can easily recommend this box if you need to "fan-out" a single HDMI input port to five independent signal sources. It does exactly what it says -- you control which input is selected, without the box trying to automatically switch to whichever input line is "active". The remote works well and the overall hook-up and operation is simple and straight forward. Overall device quality seemed very good and packaging for shipment was good. I could not detect any added audio or HD video signal deterioration/distortion. The instructions are fairly adequate, just remember to pull the plastic insulating tape out of the back of the remote to allow the battery to make internal electrical contact to start the remote! This was not mentioned in the instruction sheet of the unit I received.

I can understand why some reviewers have complained that the power and selected channel indicator LED's are too bright and are distracting. My solution was to put a 3.5 inch strip of gray electrical tape across the front of the unit. The gray is less obtrusive than the white electrical tape that I tried, and does it a better job of taming the LED's output. You get a diffuse lighted dot to indicate "power on" and the channel that is "on", and can neatly write the name of the signal for the channels on it [e.g. DVD, Fire Stick, Computer, Game, etc.] with a Ultra Fine Point permanent marker pen. Put a 3.5 inch strip of Scotch Magic Mending Tape on top to protect what you have written on the electrical tape if that is a concern.

18December2016 update -- one of the white LED's that indicates the selected channel has failed, but otherwise unit continues to work fine.

title: Great saw that packs easily.
text:
I've owned and used the smaller version of this same saw for many years. It collapses nicely and carries easily. I used to velcro it inside the hood of my snowmobile where it was always handy for light trail clearing or campfire woodcutting. Now we use it when camping in the summer. This a packable saw.

This larger one is new to me but I'm sure it will serve me just as well for a long time and, of course, handle bigger jobs.

There is 2 reasons I don't give this saw 5 stars. First, I haven't used it yet. Second is the wing nut that holds the blade to the handle during use and keeps the saw together when folded and stowed. There is nothing that stops the wing nut from loosening up and potentially falling off and getting lost. I drilled a hole in 1 wing of the wing nut and a hole in the threaded shaft and use a piece of wire threaded through both to keep the wing nut on the rod and not get lost while folded up and traveling. That's its only real drawback. If you loose that wing nut and don't have another, the saw is nearly useless.

title: Erik Larson leaves us wanting more...
text:
I read Erik Larson's book with great curiosity and high expectations, given the stellar reviews it has received in the media and academia. After finishing it, I have to admit I was torn between contradictory feelings:
- on one hand, the research is exhaustive and the reconstruction of the time he covers (basically July 1933-June 1934) is awesome, with great character depiction and an amazing ability to make intrigues in the State Department and events in Berlin come alive.
- on the other hand, the book left me deeply frustrated for at least 2 major reasons:

1) some major questions are left completely unanswered, esp. was Martha Dodd a Soviet spy? How did her obvious promiscuity not constitute more of an issue for the State Department, her father or a vulnerability to the German secret services?

2) even more importantly, what happens after the Night of the Long Knives (June 30, 1934)??? Dodd stayed in post until December 1937, i.e. another three and a half years (!) but barely a word is said about events during that time and his role in the American reaction to these events.

I would understand this silence if nothing had happened between June 1934 and the Anschluss, but there were extraordinary events that deserved at least a mention:
- the assassination of the Austrian chancellor Engelbert Dollfuss, which led to major tension between Germany and Italy, and took place less than a month after the June 1934 "epilogue" to the book
- the Saar referendum in January 1935
- the introduction of the Nuremberg laws in September 1935
- the referendum and remilitarization of Rhineland in March 1936
- the start of the Spanish Civil war in July 1936
All of these events were major milestones in the accession of Hitler to absolute power and the unstoppable march towards a world war, and it is unthinkable that Dodd (or Larson for that matter) has nothing to say about them... If the sources or archival materials dried up after Dodd's first year in Germany, why doesn't Larson tell us so and explain why he covers only the first 22% or so of his tenure as US ambassador !!!

Overall, a great read, but one that barely scratches the surface of a fascinating subject.

title: First impression and spooling line on the 2000 model.
text:
First impression:
- Body looks solid.
- if you can get it for about $20.00, you can't really complain, it's no $100 reel nor $200.00 but It will do the job.
- it's a good throw away, travel, back up reel at that price that can handle big fish. I would recommend spending more if you want something nicer but it would cost 2 or 3 times more.
-2000 spool size is too big. It's comparable to a 4000 spool. It's much deeper than a 2000. If I had to do it again I'll try for the 1000 instead for most applications.
- the line clip as shown on the picture fell off probably 3 times when messing with it at home or just spooling it. (I will probably try to glue the clip that holds it down together underneath before I end up losing it.) Highly recommend checking that all screw are tighten properly, you wouldn't want to loose any screw.
- the drag jumps from 33lb to no drag or 2/3lbs in about 10 clicks or a 90 degree dial turn. It's not very sensitive, it adjust at about 2/3lbs increments per clicks. You will probably need to set your drag gently to match your line if you do not want the line to snap under pressure for lighter lines. The drag is not ideal if you want to achieve a certain adjustable drag while fishing. Your drag might be too loose or too tight.
- line lay isn't impressive. It's ok at best just as shown. Not even. But it's only $20.00. When you fill pass 60%, it's hard not to get a few loose wrap. Tried to respool it couple times, I still have a few loose wrap every time. If you are picky and keep it under 60% you might be ok.

My guess is this reel will do the job for most applications and big fishes. The drag seems as if it will have very little to no play for some applications.

I will update after testing it enough on the water.

title: A page turner, but dissapointing
text:
With her ususal excellent style and story telling skills, Ruth Rendell introduces us to a petty criminal and the effect he has on several of his victoms--lonely, vulnerable women. Somewhere in the middle of the novel, by an unfortunate (or fortunate) coincidence he meets his death in a moveie theater by the hand of a former victim. The second part is dedicated to the effect this deathhas on his victims. As usual in Rendell's novels, we are exposed to her much praised talent to draw in fine psycological detail her charcaters. Because of that, Rendell's novels carry some form of social significance that take them beyond the mystery level. And as usual, this book is a page turner.
However, in this particular novel, she has too many characters and, respectively, too many social issues/implications going on that do not always come together as planned. We have a gay MP that is relevied when he is forced to come out (social responsibiltry vs. personal freedom), his wife who is not necessarily a bad mother to her kids, but still really dumb (feminist ideas vs. traditional upbringing dilemmas); a couple with opposite eating disorders that somehow get cured abd their relationship with their friend who unvoluntarily implcates them in a crime (friednship and betrayal); and all of the above are not related too much to the mystery. I just felt that she has tried to put everything into a single book leaving a lot of the questions she raises unresolved...

text: Ok, so this review is long over due, but I figure, sometimes that's what we need to see in order to know that the product is doing it's job, right? So...with that said, I absolutely love these hanging file folders. I even suggest that you will need to order more than one pack if you've got a lot of things to file away. If you're like me, you consider paying a little extra for the colored, pocketed ones that have slits to put thumb tags on them. That way you can organize your stuff according to title/color, for instance, all my banking papers and statements are filed under the yellow folders tagged "banking" and all the insurance papers are in red folders tagged "car insurance, health insurance," etc., and so on. Color coding makes things easier to identify, always, as opposed to seeing those bland green or manila folders in the drawer and you've got to thumb through them for awhile before you find the folder you're looking for. And there's so much room in these folders to condense your bills, papers, and things, that with my cell phone bills, I can nearly hold up to 4 years worth, and counting, within one folder!!! The folders are pretty sturdy with their metal sliding holders and can withstand the weight and/or the wear-n-tear of you pulling them out of the drawer and filling them every month or so. Also, the accordian-like stretchiness on the sides make them easy to condense or fill. My folders have been holding up for at least 2 years now and I'm sure they'll last me a life-time. I prefer getting these and filling up my metal filing cabinets with them as opposed to getting those plastic, flimsy filers that stand alone or come in plastic totes. text:
I love Crystal, she's a character I was super excited for & I'm still rlly excited to see her in the movie. I think her doll is beautiful, she has a stunning face, beautiful hair, and a cute outfit. However, I should point out that she doesn't look like she does in the stock photo. Her skin isn't sparkly, the blue paint on her crown is much more subdued, there's no paint on her scepter or shoes, and you can tell the colors on the photo have been altered, which I find odd since Crystal's color scheme is really beautiful, and it's probably the best thing she has going for her.

I can rlly only give this doll 4 stars on account of the fact that her artwork pictures a belt and necklace that do not appear on the doll. I think these would have rlly tied her look together. I'm also disappointed by the lack of stand and diary with this doll. Diaries were always a super interesting insight into the character, and it would be a shame if they're getting rid of those completely. In favor of a silly little ring. She does have molded leggings, which doesn't personally bother me since I never redress my dolls, but I know for a lot of people this is a big negative. There's also no brush, which again doesn't bother me personally.

So overall, I think she's a great doll. But is she worth $20? No way. I'd recommend waiting for her to go on clearance if you want her & don't want to overpay.

text:
The WANTED story arc begins to tie together many elements that have been percolating since the first issue. Barbara Gordon, aka Batgirl, has been on a long road of building herself up mentally ever since her physical recovery from her previous spinal injury from getting shot in the spine by the Joker, that had her in a wheelchair for two years and then a full third year of physical rehab.

This volume shows us Barbara at her darkest before the proverbial dawn, and when she ignites her self-confidence, then Batgirl is a terror to behold for the criminal underworld of Gotham! But writer Gail Simone shows us the VERY human character underneath all the super hero get-up, and it's this emotional resonance that readers have really taken to. I am very happy to have the WANTED story arc all placed together into one volume, it's one of the strongest Batgirl stories in possibly her entire history in print.

title: The plight of the Third World
text:
Accomplished master of the police procedural Henning Mankell strays from this genre in his latest novel, "Kennedy's Brain". In his novel, Mankell in the guise of a mystery, has penned what is in reality a social commentary. Mankell who resides at least partially in Mozambique, takes aim at the plight of the African underprivileged particularly relating to the AIDS epidemic and it's exploitation by the pharmaceutical companies.

Swedish archaeologist Louise Cantor whose specialty is ancient Greek artifracts is leading an expedition in Greece sponsored by Uppsala university. She happily anticipates taking a break to return to Stockholm and visit her son Henrik. Much to her shock and dismay she arrives at his flat, unable to raise him on the phone, to find him lying dead in bed. She is stunned to learn that an autopsy confirms that he overdosed on barbiturates.

Unable to believe that Henrik would take his own life she commences her own investigation. She travels across the world to a remote area of Australia to recruit her estranged husband Aron and inform him of their son's death. Together they go through his papers that direct them to an apartment their son kept in Barcelona. Hacking into his computer they discover that he was HIV positive and that he had business that took him to Mozambique.

Louise Cantor proceeds to Africa after the mysterious disappearance of her ex husband. While there she is confronted by danger and the horrors of a village designed to care for AIDS victims where Henrik had worked. She discovers that there is quite a bit more going on there than administering to the sick.

Mankell paints a graphic picture of the misery endured by the suffering in Africa while being critical of those who opportunistically use them for financial gain. The plot of "Kennedy's Brain", metaphor for an inexplicable and secretive mystery is very much similar to Le Carre's "The Constant Gardener".

title: Read THE TAMING before this one...
text:
PREQUEL: THE TAMING
Awww now. Once again this book reminded of why I have Jude Deveraux's name in one of my top 3 favorite author list. She is definitely gifted with words and know how to implement her very own heart soaring ideas. The lovable characters, the intriguing plot from the prequel of this book, THE TAMING, continues here in THE CONQUEST with much added exciting twist and some newly introduce charming characters.
There's 3 reasons why I didn't rate this book a fiver. One is because of the speedy conclusion of this wondeful SAGA. It was rushed and seemed uncomplete for me. Perhaps there is another book in the making to explain this kind of ending.... but if there's none, then I am sorely disappointed. I wanted at least an EPILOGUE with confirmation of decisions and etc. or a short extension of all the character's whereabouts and future. You'll know why and what I mean once u read THE TAMING and THE CONQUEST.
Two, I also wished Severn have his own story. I was not satisfied with his short-add-on story here in THE CONQUEST. Lady Anne is indeed a great match for Severn and I really would love to read more of them. I also would have enjoyed reading Iolanthe's appearance in Lady Anne and Severn's life. Again, you'll need to read THE TAMING and THE CONQUEST to know what I mean.
Third, I also would have love to see people's reaction to Zared's transformation from the BOY squire to a Lady. What of Ralph and Colbrand? Wouldn't it be fun to read their reaction?
Despite that three complains of mine, this book still manage to be a 4 stars to me because it did bring out lots of emotional helter-skelter in me... I love the way Tearle reaches out to Zared. His ways of courtship and his gentleness towards her. I sighed for Zared cuz I can see through her heart and understand her desires and confusions. The long awaited answers to the puzzles and mystery is not to be missed... but most of all, this book made me laugh. It's a grand book links.... Read to know what I mean!

title: Gotta love Mia Scalisi!!
text:
Princes of the Lower East Side by Meredith Allison is the second book in the Scalisi family series. I think I liked this book even better than the first!

It takes off just after the first ends where Mia is spending time with her family in Scilly, relaxing on the beach enjoying her blood oranges and talks with retired gangsters.

When Mia and her sister-in-law Gloria come back to New York she discovers so much has changed. Not just in her old neighborhood, Little Italy, but with the business her brother left behind.

Who can Mia trust? Her business partners? Charlie? She has a contract signed, so the show must go on, but she can't just let her brothers business go down the toliet, can she?

This book really blew me away! It was detailed, the characters where written incredibly well. I loved Mia, her spirit, her drive, her love of family, and her williness to compromise when necessary. Meredith Allison's Scalisi family series is a treasure! Absolutely read both books if you haven't already!!

title: Outstanding little pump at fair price/switch is questionable
text:
UPDATE: April 2016 -- I've been using this pump for a little over a year and the pump, itself, continues to function well but I'm beginning to have problems with the float switch. The switch now turns the pump on in the full off position but, if I raise it I/2 inch, it turns off. It will restart gain at about 1 1/2 inches up or floating. I've managed to keep it working by holding it above the full off position with a rope but I'm now concerned that the rope will float away and the pump will run until it burns up or destroys the battery by running it until it is totally discharged. It appears to find a quality float switch, I'll have to spend about as much for the switch as I have for the switch and pump combo and the add-on pump. I'm still very pleased with the pump. It does what it's supposed to and does it well.

This is a strong pump for its small size and low cost. It took about fifteen minutes to pump out a twelve foot Portabote that was three quarters full of water and it's worked without fail since I installed it to keep the boat rain water free. At just over $20 for the pump and switch with an additional backup pump as a $5 add-on, this is a super bargain. So far both pump and switch have proven to be reliable but they're not designed for heavy duty use and I would not think of using them in situations where the vessel will be unattended for a long period of time or when large volumes of water need to be dealt with. While the pump can clear a significant amount of water quickly, it's really designed for light incidental use. I'm very happy with this purchase because I believe that I'm using the pump and switch as they were intended...in a non-critical situation to handle incidental rainwater and spray. To ask them to do much more could be asking for trouble.

title: A shamanic journey
text:
In this seventh instalment of Stoner's (and friends') adventures, Stoner and her business partner Marylou have moved their travel agency from Boston to Shelburne Falls. This small New Age town is perfect for Aunt Hermione's psychic activities and a new start for teacher Gwen, Stoner's life partner. But is seventy-five-year-old Hermione eventually getting old, or is her forgetfulness caused by hungry ghosts trying to steal her soul? It is up to reluctant believer Stoner to take a shamanic journey and save her aunt.

While previously her adventures mostly involved down-to-earth detective work on the side, Stoner is no stranger to shamanic journeying ('Grey Magic') and has even experienced time travel ('Captive in Time'). However she'd rather have a normal day-to-day life even if she feels like something is missing, despite Gwen's devoted love.

'Shaman's Moon' carries the trademark humour and feminist ideas of the Stoner McTavish series, even if no one is perfect. This volume, first published in 1998, is infused with light touches of philosophy and a dose of Native-American spirituality. It is captivating and colourful, and I guess would be pivotal in the series if Sarah Dreher had written more. I believe there is an 8th volume ('Love Murders'), but it is out of print or unavailable.

Sadly the author died in spring 2012. I'll be forever grateful to Sarah Dreher for creating one of my favourite fictional characters: the neurotic –but lovable, and forever hypothesizing too much, Stoner McTavish, a womon weary of cats, devoted to her aunt Hermione, passionately in love with her partner Gwen, and generally understanding of her best friend Marylou.

title: It's not about food
text:
Differently from the movie, this is not a tale about sophisticated food. It deals with the severe restrictions that puritanism imposes on pleasure - and how a tastefull dinner, with the help of some good wines, helps this fundamentalist lutheran aging community to retrieve joy and forgiveness.

In the movie, although the puritan restrictions are present, stress is on the food - the ingredients, the way it is being prepared, the discovery of it by the coachman and Bebette's assitant, and principally the precise description by the general. The transformation of the puritans, from mere tolerance of an extravagance to real appreciation and joy only underines the quality of what is being served.

In the novel, food plays a secondary role, contrasting with the grey sad environment and the equally gray and sad inhabitants of a norwegian community lost in the high north, squeezed between the mountains and an unfriendly see. Stress is on the way a severe pastor has molded the spirit of his daughters and of his few followers, banning all earthly pleasures.

I've decided to read the novel after having a dinner that reproduced the menu of Babette's feast, preceded by the film and a technical explanation by the danish chef. Dinner was excelent and our community did not resemble at all to the inhabitants of the small village - which in the film was moved from Norway to Denmark. I was first surprised by the differences in approach but then I realized that this short novel gives you food for thoughts. While the movie is pure pleasure, the novel is profound.

I recommend it and, if I may suggest, have it complete: the movie, the dinner and the short novel.

title: Inspiring

Loving thoughts and expressions for my wife, and as a Minister, I have found several passages here than can be altered slightly to fit quite nicely in wedding ceremonies.

The writing here is a good as anything I've read on the expression of love and Douglas Pagels and Blue Mountain books are both to be commended for this fine work. If you have difficulty finding the right words to express your love to that special someone in your life, this book will certainly guide you in the right direction. You'll find thoughts and poems that can easily be altered to fit your circumstances, or in many cases, presented verbatim.

If you think there are just no new ways to express love, think again.

title: "Poems so women will escape illusion, resignation, descent"
text:
If variety is indeed a spice, this fine collection of poetry has been tastefully blended. Featuring several dozens of different poets with multifarious voices spanning the centuries from age-old folksy rhymes and sublime Buddhist hymns to stridently vocal contemporary verse, all rendered into English (side by side with the original Vietnamese) with veritable sensitivity by an assembly of various translators and collaboratively arranged by an American & Vietnamese team of editors, this entry in the "Defiant Muse" series really stands out. No two poems feel the same, even as all of them vividly address and explore women's experiences in their own distinct and compelling words.

Furthermore, a substantial introduction accessibly providing proper historical context for the poems and explaining their place in the rich Vietnamese literary tradition plus a handy and sufficiently detailed biographical guide to each poet properly situates the collection's selections, making this book a reliable study and reference as well. Highly recommended!

title: Well Done Expose' On The Radical Right
text:
This book is part muckraking,part psyhcological analysis of the extreme right that has taken over the Republican Party.
Mr. Blumenthal did a large amount of research in this journalistic endeavor and he added a section at the end of the book to cover the first year of the Obama administration.

One Eisenhower quote that seldom gets mentioned is found in the Introduction, it's a warning and it's not about the military-industrial complex.
"His admonition to beware the danger posed to democracy by those who seek 'freedom from the necessity of informing themselves and making up their own minds concerning these tremendous complex ands difficult questions.'"
That is a tool used quite effectively by the conservative media apparatus.

One of the intriguing subjects in "Republican Gomorrah" was the discovery of Sarah Palin, who discovered her, how and what they did to promote her.
Another is the general history of the religious right on homosexuality and hypocrisy.
Contrasting the downfall of Larry Craig and Ted Haggard with conservatives like David Vitter and Newt Gingrich.
Added to the mix is the "kingmaker" that believes his endorsement is essential for any potential Republican presidential candidate.
Look too deeply into the conservative religious right and you see double-standards and lots of activity that runs counter to Scripture.
On page 42 the author writes "Under Reconstructionist rules of engagement, lying, deception, and stealth are considered legitimate tactics and are even encouraged."

This book is thoroughly documented and is a fast read. More important is what it exposes in the Republican Party and how that element wormed it's way in.
This is a fairly current work and one that every American voter should read.

title: A Colorful Spectrum of Poetry and Painting
text:
Victoria Franks paints pictures with oil and with words, each complementing the other. Her book of poetry and art The Aroma of Coffee is colorful and sensual. From the mountains of South America and the deserts of Arizona to the swamps and shores of Northwest Florida, Franks details the unique beauty she perceives.
Her work covers the gamut of pride in country and despair at war and loneliness to passion, love, and joy. Her poetry shows us the simple yet difficult life of Columbians alongside the complexities of their struggle. Every topic she covers resounds with insightful truth.
Flavored with chocolate, potatoes and corn, mojitos and margaritas, the aroma of coffee is merely a tease. Her work is colored with every hue of the spectrum and accented with Spanish words that roll off the tongue as well as the page, their English definition less important than their fluidity.
Readers easily see the pictures of her words and infer the meanings just below the surface of her paintings. Franks travels effortlessly from one medium to the other and takes the reader with her.

title: A Must-Have
text:
The authors offer truly groundbreaking insights and methods in this book, and I will cite a few, but the depth and breadth of their work is far too vast to encapsulate here. They note the plethora of unhelpful, anecdotal advice that often passes for wisdom in similar books, and instead provide scientifically documented, step-by-step methods for defining and achieving goals. They provide compelling examples of how these techniques have been implemented. The most fascinating story, in my opinion, involved the eradication of the guinea worm, an endemic parasite that can grow up to three feet long and emerges through the skin causing tremendous pain. The authors cited techniques employed by Carter Foundation workers to teach villagers how to filter their water and prevent reinfestation of water sources by infected persons. Carter Foundation workers sought positive deviants (villages who had learned their own ways of avoiding guinea worm infestation) to teach other villages what to do.

I noted many techniques that I myself had discovered by trial and error, such as perfect practice, which involves working on improving specific elements of a task; they cite basketball freethrowing, where perfect practice includes improving followthrough, elbow position, etc., as opposed to results oriented practice that can reinforce poor technique, e.g. shoot until I get 20 baskets. As a Chemistry teacher, I inherently implemented many of these techniques. title: Great value, particularly for the accessories
text:
Fortnite's figures are great, and collecting accessories is much of the fun, but you don't usually get many accessories with basic figures--you typically either have to buy loot chests or special/deluxe sets to get accessories. The piñatas are some of the best deals due to how many accessories you get, along with a figure. Although the MSRP of a piñata is slightly higher than the price of a single figure plus a single loot chest, you get a lot more content--over twice as many accessories as what you'd get from a standard loot chest. And not all the accessories or variations can be found in other sets--so even if you already have a decent stash of accessories, some of these will probably still be new to you.

The Rust Lord figure is not the prettiest or fanciest-looking figure in the series, but he's pretty decent. A lot of the characters are very cartoony, but this guy's design is a little bit more subdued, which may or may not be a plus depending on your tastes. Like all the 4" figures, he's got a very high amount of articulation and pretty sophisticated construction, so you'll want to be a little careful with him at first. If any joints seem stuck, try soaking him in hot water briefly to loosen them up and lessen the risk of breakage. I haven't had any problems with any of my figures yet, but be aware it can happen. I wouldn't recommend these for very young kids due to their relatively complex design.

And yes, the packaging is really a sort of piñata. It's designed for you to be able to bash it open. You can probably open it up without destroying it if you are careful. Be aware that there's a lot of confetti inside, in case you do decide to break it open.

text:
Compared to Reel/Related Products Inc flatback tape, Intertape 530 utility-grade is an okay 2nd choice. Maybe I need to try a different grade of Intertape - this being the utility grade - but so far I'm a little underwhelmed.
Intertape is 7.2 mil thick, but my old tape - Reel brand - is 7.4. Doesn't seem like much, but you can tell the difference. I question the Intertape 45 lb tensile strength claim. Reel tape says it's strength is only 32 lb, but it is tougher tape. It takes intentional effort to tear Reel tape, but Intertape tears very readily. Could be handy - if that's what you're after. If you need a lot of tensile strength in your tape, definitely go with the Reel brand.
Intertape definitely has less adhesive, but some people might find this a plus. You can reposition it - if you do it right away. Reel tape is very sticky and once it is down, it is down - you know you have a good, solid bond immediately.
I can't find Reel brand flatback retail, so I guess we'll have to settle.

title: Forget reggaeton, this is Latin alternative at its finest!
text:
Colombian Latin alternative rockeros return to form with this outstanding album. The music is so good you don't even need to understand Spanish to get it. "Complemento," "Paces" and "Al Parque"are sure to appear in a future greatest hits compilation. These musical witch doctors have been concocting just the right amount of rock, Colombian folkloric music, Andean spiritual rhythms and Afro-South American beats for the perfect potion and they've never shared it with anyone (nor has any group been able to reverse engineer it). On "Oye" it's evident they still have the recipe carefully tucked away and the potion still has magical healing powers.

Though their creative trajectory has transformed them from punks to popstars to trip-hopsters (as captured on their appropriately titled and excellent greatest hits CD, "Evolucion/Evolution"), it's the first time they appear to be basking in nostalgia and taking a step back, which isn't necessarily a bad thing if you're the Aterciopelados. And it's especially not a bad thing when the album is reminiscent of their amazing 1997 release, "Pipa de la Paz." Though on this album, you won't catch former uber feminist and vocalist Andrea Echeverri who recently became a mom singing lyrics like: "I won't ruin my silhouette with a baby" as she did on "La Culpable" off the "Pipa" album.

The Latin alternative world can also exhale. Despite the lanky Echeverri and the mousy Hector Buitrago helping each other out on both of their recent solid solo efforts, the rumors ran rampant about an imminent break-up. Though Echeverri's Latin Grammy-nominated album of her same name had a commercial edge over Buitrago's "Connector," Buitrago demonstrated that he can take some calculated artistic risks and still pull off a successful avant-garde album.

To enjoy this album you don't need Spanish. You don't even need an open mind. All you need is good taste. Enjoy! --Mario I. Oña

title: Game changer for walking my big dog

This harness keeps her in check without choking or hurting her and I like it alot. It is easy to adjust and not visibly uncomfortable to her, never chokes her. She can eat or drink with it on. Walks are much easier. By controlling her head, her pulling is inhibited and she is more prone to listen to training commands. Squirrels or other dogs still get her excited and she will pull initially but if I use a shorter grip on the leash, she obeys. When we walk and she starts to tug, I stop walking and she relents. Pulling is never zero, but it is much more brief.

Others wrote that dogs can get the harness off and yes, if I don't pay attention she has tried to push it off her nose with her paw. A little correction stops that and we continue our walks.

It doesn't appear uncomfortable but she would prefer not to have any leash on of course. I only use the trainer on a leash, she doesn't wear it all the time and when I bring out the leash for walk time, she sits and waits to get it on. I tried a pinch collar in the past, she was definitely unwillingly to have that put on and would run to her kennel instead. Contrarily, she is eager to get this harness on and go for a walk anytime.

Walks are pleasurable again and we use it daily. Highly recommend.

The Forester books nail down the action/adventure genre - not as dense as O'Brian, but well-written, compelling, and fast-moving. This Bolitho book seemed to aspire to that same action/adventure niche but came up dramatically short. I'm not exactly a purist - unpretentious action/adventure books from the 1940s-1970s are a favorite of mine. But it just wasn't good.

title: Mixed Emotions
text:
A dark and foreboding novel of a thousands years ago -- the coldness of the climate and the land accentuated by the lack of the sun's light -- although it teasingly seems to appear on the horizon to prematurely announce its impending return.

"The Wolf in the Whale" is populated by ancient, mysterious, powerful and hardy people - Norsemen and women living, fighting and dying in a new world. The whole novel brings with it a sense of perpetual cold and darkness.

The spirits seem to reign in this book -- they talk to the shamans young and old, and bestow upon them certain powers as the situations deem -- The chief protagonists are a young girl and her older brother, who use their wits to survive -- and who are transmuted back and forth to animal spirits and back again to human.

The narrative is excellent - one can feel the harsh living conditions and can be caught up in the spirit world that revolves around each person like a whirlpool of snow and cold air. The veil between the spirit, animal and human world is very thin indeed.

However, I felt that the book dragged on for too long -- and after a while this reader began to feel mired down in spots, as if walking thru a powdery snow capped with thin ice - very slow going.

So although "The Wolf in the Whale" transported me quite well, back to an era where the spirits and animals spoke with and transferred powers on primitive warrior humans fighting to survive in a cold and forbidding land - it was a wearying journey for me, as it was, IMHO, far too long.

title: Live in Gratitude (Not in Greed)
text:
Concerned about "the scary stuff" in the classical Grimm's Fairy Tales, author Susan Meredith chose to rewrite in a softer style. This 2010 soft-cover, 20 page story is nicely populated with colored illustrations on about every other page. This is a story that discourages greed and encourages love and kindness.

In our story, a simple fisherman lives by the sea with his pretty wife. He loves her deeply and works long hours to provide her with nice things to make her happy, but she was never happy. What she had was never enough. One day, he accidentally caught an enchanted flounder. Lady fish "Lorraine" was a beautiful fish with big green eyes and red eyelashes. She spoke, begging for her release, explaining that she was an enchanted princess who was never happy with what she had. She wished for more and more, until she wished too much and "poof". Now she could only grant wishes for others; nothing for herself. Because of his kindness, Lorraine offered the fisherman a wish as he returned her to the sea, but he declined, saying he had everything he needed to make him happy.

Well, you guessed it! When the fisherman returned home and told his wife, she became very angry. SHE wanted more and insisted he return to the sea and ask Lorraine for a larger house. The wife got her wish, but she continued to ask for more and more. Each time the fisherman went to see Lorraine, they chatted like friends and Lorraine granted the wish. Meanwhile, the wife acted as though her husband was no longer good enough for her and her fine house, money, and servants. On his last trip, Lorraine suggested he send his wife instead, if she still wanted more. The wife came, and as you may have guessed, she wished one wish too many and "poof".

Enchanted princess Lorraine changed back to a beautiful woman and rowed ashore to the fisherman.

Without violence or scary stuff, the story illustrates karma nicely - what goes around comes around - you reap what you sow, etc. It also encourages love and gratitude, and discourages being caught up in greed over material things.

Nice value lesson for children, written well, easy to understand, pretty to look at--a winner all around. Even my inner child enjoyed the story!

title: Research First Then Decide
text:

But this[...]side by side comparison of both from a satisfied user of both is just what I needed.

I was leaning towards the genie as being an apartment dweller carting in and out heavy bags of litter is really just killing me but the bad reviews were making me anxious about it. I can manage the litter on occasion but could I really stomach the smell of a backed up or not properly cleaned bowl? What if it backed up and didn't just sit in the bowl but overflowed? My deposit would be ruined and I'd never be able to get the sledge out of all the crannies. I think I'd rather live with any smell I get from the LR (my cat simply has stinky poo) and noise than having to clean up sludge.

title: One Compelling Book
text:
Wow! That was my first reaction to this book after just a few pages. This simply is one amazing story, and even more amazing considering the timeline of it.
Peter Maas recounts the remarkable story of the submarine, the USS Squalus, which sunk to the bottom of the North Atlantic in May of 1939. Charles "Swede" Momsen, a U.S. Navy officer, and a revolutionary scientist, was summoned to rescue these men from their watery grave.
Maas vividly depicts the tense moments involved in this heroic rescue. He uses a fast-paced language, peppered with an excellent combination of quotes and technological terms to create a very thrilling and riviting read. I almost felt as if I was part of the rescue operation myself.
Although this book kept me interested in its suspenseful voyage, the technical terms could have probably been described in a slightly more reader-friendly manner. I found myself a little confused at some times, but the overall flow of the book was still pretty smooth.
I enjoyed the epilogue quite a bit, as this small section is where the reader really gets to see the personal side of Momsen. This book was truly excellent. It was a pleasure to read. I could not put it down.

title: Adequate Brush But Buyer Beware
text:
I first purchased this brush back in 2013. After just a few shaves the brush separated from the handle and I started a return. I wanted a replacement, but it was out of stock so Simply Beautiful sent me a refund instead, without requiring me to return the defective brush. I decided to attempt a repair of the brush. After gluing it back together with marine epoxy the brush is still working fine but showing it's age through normal wear. Now five years later (2018) I decided to purchase a backup to have on hand for when the old brush becomes worn out. So I ordered a second brush thinking by now the manufacturer had probably worked out the issue. Unfortunately, again after just a few uses the new brush also separated from the handle. This time the seller, Simply Beautiful, sent me a replacement. The replacement seems to be performing fine after a few weeks of usage. So far, so good.

In summary, I like the brush. It suits my needs. But I am disappointed in the manufacturing of the product.
If you order one of these be prepared for this issue. And maybe have some Marine Epoxy on hand.

As a side note, it is not unusual for some brushes to have a "wet dog" odor when new. This can be remedied by repeatedly soaking the brush in soapy water overnight. Through normal usage the odor will eventually go away.

title: Waaay better than the Swann I replaced
text:
[[VIDEOID:7ae84ae66b1c39445d7e5289bdae27ae]] I live in a 2nd story apartment and installed a Swann 2.4GHz wireless that I picked up from the local hardware store about a year ago. I installed it after scaring off some would-be car thief's. I decided to replace it because one of my receivers went out and I replaced it with the standard Astak 2.4GHz wireless receiver. I was impressed with the receiver (w/remote) and so I thought I'd give these cameras a try (the Swann was very choppy and I had to mess with the brightness controls in the software I use, a lot). I use the second receiver to hook to the TV in my living room. The cameras and receiver are in the same location as when I was using the Swann.

These cameras are way better than the Swann. The video that comes with this review was taken from my PC (I wire it through a Roxio RCA to USB connector) and use a freeware program to capture it (Debut). There are three walls between my computer and the cameras.

Others post about bad reception because of wireless routers. I don't use one, but there are several that appear in my wireless network list on my Windows PC. To be fair, they could have changed their routers after I installed the Swann a year ago.

Downside: The audio is choppy and has static. I don't use the audio; I didn't use the audio with the Swann, either. This is the reason for my "low" marks. Also, in the manual I discovered that in low light the cameras will switch to black and white. However, as you can see from the video, the b/w hasn't switched on. There is a big flood light in my parking lot which may be the reason. Color 24/7. Judge for yourself.

Tip: you may need to adjust the antenna on the receiver to get the lowest amount of static. I've found that moving it about 20 degrees at a time lets you see the difference.

Well worth the money. I hope this helps.

title: The "gateway drone" for beginners
text:
I've never owned a drone before so didn't know what to expect. This package contains two zippable pouches with a folded controller and drone, which are both tiny. You have to charge both units before attempting anything, and the charging station isn't obvious to use. Next, install the app on your phone and it will sync with the drone later.

Once unfolded, there is a calibration process you must follow before flying, which is a minor inconvenience but you learn the routine pretty quickly. The controller has a number of directional buttons but the easiest way to learn is to go outside in a large, clear area and experiment - after about an hour of flight time, you can get very proficient with the joysticks.

The unit broadcasts video back to your phone (or records to the provided SD card) and it's entertaining to watch your flight experience. This is not a stabilized gimbal so don't expect SteadiCam-style gliding - it can get a little rough at times - and there's no audio.

The machine will hover by itself with very little drift, and the return to home button works well. There is an option to use indoors but it's not a great idea - I decapitated a houseplant, nipped on my fingers and almost destroyed a light fixture. Without the GPS (and in the hands of a novice), indoor flying isn't particularly safe.

This drone is a good unit for beginners, older kids and supervised children, and can get you used to the basics of how drone operation works. After a few flights, you'll find yourself wanting to upgrade to something more expensive with more features, but at this price level it's a great way to learn the ropes.

There are dozens, maybe hundreds of good Mediterranean cookbooks out there, and one that is excellent and includes a huge number of recipes for variety is 1000 Mediterranean Meals: Every Recipe You Need for the Healthiest Way to Eat by Valentina Harris. This cookbook has everything: appetizers, side dishes, soups, salads, mains with or without meat and even desserts. Although they are touted as healthier dishes, they are still mouthwatering, and no one will suspect that eating them will contribute to better health.

Almost all of the recipes include a photograph, which makes the book appealing. Most cooks want to know what the dish should look like. The recipes are written in the classic style with a list of ingredients and easy-to-follow instructions that cooks at all levels can successfully make them.

The variety of the dishes is vast, and there is something for every taste. Most of the recipes include several variations to that everyone can individualize them to their personal tastes. The recipes come from several of the twenty-one countries that border the Mediterranean Sea. Popular classics are included, such as Hummus and Tzatziki, as well as some unique dishes like Huevos Revueltos and Egyptian Sweet Couscous.

Anyone who likes Mediterranean food will love reading and cooking from this excellent cookbook. There will be dozens of recipes that appeal to almost every cook.

Special thanks to NetGalley for supplying a review copy of this book.

text: When a book is released around the time of an author's death the literary world seems to shower him/her with an insane amount of praise that one has to wonder if death didn't come calling would would this book be so highly praised.  This is a short book (only about 244 pages which is slightly misleading because of page margins and text size this book is much shorter).  It's plot is compelling and it is wonderfully descriptive.  I found  Matthiessen' s tendency to switch between writing from the point of view of the main character to casual observer confusing and wish he would have stuck to one or the other.  The main character's purpose for being in this place and time (when you finally learn why)  is a great and equally tragic story line and by itself is enough to carry the reader.  The introduction of all minor characters just dilutes the story and introduces a bunch of characters that we don't care about and have absolutely no reason to care about.  Overall I gave this book 3 stars simply because the cast of characters and their relationship to the story is unmoving and distracting from the good aspects of this book.  It would be silly to tell someone not to read this book because the reality is, this is such a short book that even if you hated it you're not investing a huge chunk of your time.  It's not like reading a 1,000 page epic like PILLARS OF THE EARTH where if you hate it or get bored you've still got hundreds of pages to get through before you can properly decide what you're overall opinion is.

title: Useless for techies
text:
I'm a developer building a company-internal website and I'm struggling to organize all the information it will contain. I bought this book hoping to ease that struggle. What I found is for a technical person like me, this book was so useless that it has compelled me to write my first Amazon review in years.

I planned to read it cover to cover. After 50 pages I realized that I haven't really read anything at all yet. So far it's been ridiculously verbose, rambling, and content-free. So I gave up and started skimming.

I couldn't find much better in the remaining pages. Page after page of touchy-feely gobbledygook that has not helped me organize information at all.

There are more useless diagrams in this book than I've ever seen before. For example, the term "synonym ring" is defined as a group of words with the same meaning. Does it really take a diagram with a bunch of arrows in a circle to explain that? (Figure 9-2)

To explain the concept of equivalence we have another diagram: "A=B" inside a circle. (Figure 9-21) Does such a diagram really enhance anybody's understanding of the concept of equivalence? Why does this diagram even exist in the first place?

Maybe some business or consultant type might get something out of this book. For a developer, run away. Fast.

title: An Amish Love
text:
"An Amish Love" is a compilation of 3 novellas centering around 3 different people living in Amish civilizations. Written by Kelly Long, "A Marriage of the Heart" tells the story of Rachel Yoder, an Amish girl who has been raised by her strict father after her mother's death. Tired of her father's and the Amish rules, Yoder quickly marries Joseph Lambert, an Amish man who has only recently returned to the Plain way. Long tells Yoder's story of falling in love with her husband and facing her demons. "What the Heart Sees" by Kathleen Fuller tells the story of Ellie Chupp, a young Amish woman who lost her sight as well as her best friend in a horrible accident. When her best friend's former fiance shows up, Ellie's attempts to deal with her disability are disrupted. However, love is just around the corner for Ellie. "Healing Hearts" by Beth Wiseman tells the story of Naaman and Levina Lapp. After 30 years of marriage, they are facing an empty nest, which is something that Naaman especially cannot deal with. He leaves for year, but when he returns he finds that things are not as he hoped they would be. Levina is cold and confused, dealing with whether or not she can trust the man who left her.

I found these three novellas to be enjoyable. Easy to read and interesting, they offer insight to the lives of the Amish, as well as insight into the lives of people in general. The stories are heartwarming and touching, and I would definitely recommend the book.

The unit is BIG, though. Maybe not bigger than others, but much bigger than my old printer. If you're a work-at-home guy like me, you should measure your area before bying any of these units.

title: Chop Suey Culture
text:
If you like Chinese food, you should read this book. It will tell you everything you should have wondered about chop suey, fortune cookies, the Chinese restaurant industry and the Chinese people who have brought more than food to the United States

Ms. Lee uses her healthy curiosity and excellent research skills to study something we generally take for granted -- Chinese food is so unbiquitous as to be invisible, except when we're hungry. Being the daughter of Chinese immigrants and a New York Times reporter gives Ms. Lee the right lenses for studying her subject and produces insights that are subtle, interesting and thought-provoking. For example: How best to know the actual output of a Chinese restaurant when thinking about buying it? Count the garbage bags in the alley. Why were did Chinese laundries and restaurants survive 19th Century bigotry against the Chinese? Because cooking and washing were women's work and didn't threaten the white male labor force.

Equally as good as Ms. Lee's insights is her writing style. She has a tone that is a bit ironic, a bit whimsical. She appreciates the goofiness of what she is investigating, but also treats the topic respectfully. These are fine balances for a writer to maintain. And she brings many of her points home with a tidy turn of phrase: "Young professionals loved the idea that food could come from a phone rather than a stove." Or, "Common wisdom from one culture is perplexing in another." Or, finally, by describing American soy sauce as a "Frankensauce chemical counterfeit."

text:
When I first began this series, I was afraid I would not enjoy going back into Tortall's history, without any of the characters that have been the anchor of the Tortall series. However, I was pleasantly surprised to find myself enjoying the books, and the story that revolves around Beka Cooper, George Cooper's ancestor, and guardswoman for the Provost's Guards. It gives a clear picture of the difficulties of the lives of people with no advantages and very little opportunity.

In Bloodhound, Beka is in Port Caynn, searching for the origin of the counterfeited coins that have been popping up in Corus. While the story is enjoyable, the length is not. By page 400, I was wishing that I was at the last page. The end seems to drag on without any resolution. It doesn't help that 'Beka' keeps writing in her diary that she is tired and must stop writing. I would think at her age and maturity, she wouldn't feel the need to write in her diary as if she were talking to it.
The final aspect that was irritating was the very casual, nonchalant way Pounce was disposed of from the list of characters. It was very poorly done, and he was inserted back into the story just as poorly.

As a final thought, would Beka laugh at the irony of knowing that her descendants would have the blood of Trebond as well?

The problem I experienced is the Bluetooth mode turning off and on for no reason. Initially this would occur once or twice, and then it would play without any problems for the rest of the time it was used. Approximately one week after the problem started, it worsened, and became very frustrating. I tried resetting the speaker, and I also reloaded or re-installed the firmware, but no change.

I really thought I purchased the best mini-Bluetooth speaker out there. And never came even close to putting the Tough speaker to the test, as I had always treated it gently. It died and crapped-out all on it's own design and build quality.

When I contacted Fugoo via email, they returned a response within a few hours. I explained the problem, and was informed that I needed to replace the speaker unit. They requested proof that I purchased from an authorized dealer, and proof of date of purchase to show proof speaker was within the warranty period (12 months). Not the best way to treat a customer, especially considering the product line itself is less than the warranty period.

After I provided the requested information, I was informed that it would take 2 to 3 weeks and that I would be sent an RMA number. This was just over a 1 week ago, and I'm still waiting for the RMA number. No mention on how long I'd have to wait for an RMA, hopefully not an additional 2 to 3 weeks.

I anticipate getting a refurbished unit that crapped out on someone else. I won't be too happy about that, as mine was practically brand new, and pampered. Someday after I get the replacement, I'll do a follow up.

title: Brlliant, funny, and even a bit disturbing
text:
"Dreams of the Rarebit Fiend" is McCay's overlooked masterpiece. "Little Nemo" gets all the press (and it deserves the highest possible praise) but The Fiend is often equally compelling. More adult in subject matter than Nemo, it is less visually resplendant, but still quite powerful in its invocation of the fears and hopes underlying our day-to-day thoughts.

This collection is the standard, but it collects only a fraction of what McCay produced (this is a reprint of a 1905 volume, but the strip ran until 1910 or 1911). You can pick up the Checker "Early Works" volumes for a more complete run (in questionable quality) and there are more strips in the Canemaker book on McCay as well as the Fantagraphics "Daydreams and Nightmares" (which I highly recommend).

Checker has since produced a fine collection: [[ASIN:1933160659 The Saturdays]] which would make a great follow-up to this book.

When I first wrote this review in 2006, I pleaded for someone to do this strip justice with a comprehensive reprint. Little did I know that Ulrich Merkl was, in fact, working on one at the time. You can search the web for his "The Complete Dream of the Rarebit Fiend" ([...]). I highly reccommend it, though it is a bit pricey. Amazon now lists it here: [[ASIN:3000207511 The Complete Dreams of the Rarebit Fiend]]

title: Amstaff mom approved!!!!
text:
This collar is a life saver!
We have a nearly one year old American Amstaff that is the single most stubborn hard headed dog in the entire world. After paying ungodly amounts of money on training & behavior classes, we were at wits end with our boy. Any time we let him out the door he would take off like his tail was on fire & it was nearly impossible to get him to come back until he was good and ready. This collar has made a gigantic improvement in his behavior outside. We don't even normally have to use the shock function. Most of the time the vibrate option scares him into action & works perfectly.

The packaging was great, while there were little to no instructions in the product box, or on the box, with a little trial & error we figured it out pretty quickly.
The charger seems to work amazing. As instructed I charged the unit for 6 hours after opening. We've been using the collar for about a 1-2 weeks now and it's STILL RUNNING on THAT FIRST CHARGE! Granted we only use the collar for potty & outside time. So that's probably a big factor in our extended battery life.

We haven't had any issues with the collar itself. My pupper is a very broad Amstaff so his neck girth is pretty substantial, and the collar included fit with plenty of room to spare. We also have not had any skin issues with where the prongs sit on our boy. Again, he doesn't continuously wear the collar, which is probably a contributing factor. I could see where the prongs could potentially be an issue if the use of the unit wasn't closely supervised. Leaving it on your dog for long periods of time, in the same spot, without adjusting could definitely be hazardous to a dog.

All in all, we absolute live this collar. It was extremely affordable and a great quality for the price. Honestly, I'm surprised it's not higher. Great purchase.

title: Audience
text:
I finished reading Supreme Court Justice Stephen Breyer’s book titled, The Authority of the Court and the Peril of Politics, thinking about his intended audience. If his audience is the informed American citizen, his claims of the court not being political come across as naïve. If his audience is his fellow justices and his message is for them not to overreach because they may find the authority of the court diminished, that made a bit more sense to me. I thought of Alan Greenspan’s confession about his foundational error in the runup to the financial crisis. He assumed that banks would act prudently as a form of self-preservation. As we know, they didn’t. Why Breyer might expect fellow justices to preserve the authority of the Supreme Court by not overreaching in their decisions, I can’t imagine. We will all watch the exercise of power and learn how much peril can be absorbed by our democratic republic.

title: A Pop Up Book to Explore with Several Senses
text:
In our family, we have loved pop-up books for several generations, including examples from more than a century ago that are beloved volumes on our bookshelf to this day. While this third book has zero holiday content, we immediately recognized ABC Pop-Up as a marvelous choice for holiday gift-giving.

This pop-up book brilliantly invites adults and children to explore several senses: sound, vision and even tactile experiences of exploring the pop up shapes!

My favorite sequence is a pop-up bed that stands up in front of us, as we read the book, without any immediate clue as to the letters involved. Then, if we closely examine the bed, we discover the pillow has an embossed P in one corner and the quilt has an embossed Q. Little fingers can touch the letters and actually feel the raised shapes.

Then, the sequence continues with a stately tree that leaps up with an attached tire swing and, as we look over the entire page, we discover that we can glimpse the tree’s gnarled roots at the bottom of the page. What letters are we discovering? The tire swing actually dangles from a string and, if our eyes are quick, we can see the S for swing. But what about R? Little fingers can detect an embossed R in the tree’s roots. And then what’s the T? Well, you can guess.

In our family collection, we now own more than 100 pop up books and, while this book is, indeed, little in its physical scale, it is truly a work of genius!

title: Finally, a wired adapter that works with my Insignia Roku TV
text:
Have a Roku TV that is supposed to be wireless-only (why can't they include an rj45 jack anyway?). Even with a wireless router positioned right behind it, still had problems with adaptive streaming sites changing resolution streams multiple times during playback. Searched Roku forums and found an older Belkin adapter mentioned, but that's not available, and has a replacement listed that did not work for me. My son had purchased an HDE adapter for his Wii some time ago (and neglected to tell me), so I tried that and it did work with my TV. so I got one of those, too. Don't know if it was just defective, but the new one didn't work, neither on my TV or the Wii, or even on a laptop, so back it went. Still searching, because I proved to myself that something could work. Finally found this brand mentioned as working after another search, even though the seller says it doesn't. At this point, for $12 I figured what the heck. And it worked... With the other adapters not working I had tried everything, resetting to original settings, unplugging and re-plugging power, USB slot, Cat 6 cable, nothing.

With this adapter, all I had to do was unplug the power cord after installing, plug it back in, turn it on, and it worked. A little slower initial boot, but that's pretty minor to have a working wired connection with no more adaptive streaming fluctuations. Before, Netflix thought i only had 4 Mbps down on a good day, and afterward, that had tripled (according to the test in their app). With another separate speed test app, I'm actually getting as high as 54 Mbps down (out of 60 possible) now.

Edit, 6 weeks later, still using it every day, still working fine except for one incident where it didn't connect after a power on, but I just removed power again and restarted, and has been OK since.
