text: Okay--so there's a heartbeat to fiction, any fiction, long or short.  Beat: Exposition.  Beat: Rising Action.  Beat: Climax.  Beat: Falling action.  And in good, thoughtful fiction the falling action revisits the exposition and something has changed about the characters or the circumstances of the conflict--hopefully in all three.  I enjoyed Micah--I did.  He wasn't my favorite character, and now I like him more, and since I intend to continue reading this seminal series, that's a good thing, because he's become a big part of it.  In a way, reading this work was sort of like getting to know a brother in law you thought was just set decoration and finding out he's got a good sense of humor or something.  The problem with the novella was, that Anita, our main character, didn't seem to come to this--or any--conclusion about this character by the end of the story.  I needed to see some sort of reflection about Micah, about her acceptance of him in her life, in her bed, and instead, we jumped out of a (admittedly hot and character, uhm, building) sex scene, and into the metaphysics and although both parts were fun, there was no emotionally satisfying wrap up.  At the end, it was just Micah and Nathaniel and that's it, folks-- he's just set decoration again when we'd really started to think of him as a friend.  I still love this series, and I still like these characters, but this smaller installment was missing something vital.  It was missing a heartbeat.

title: A fantastic thriller!
text:
THE VACATION by T.M. Logan primarily follows Kate, a wife and mother of two meeting up with her three best friends and their families at a stunning vineyard villa in France for a vacation to celebrate their 40th birthdays. It is meant to be a time to reconnect with each other and their families with good wine, good food and good company. Things aren’t starting off on an ideal note, however.

Kate has a feeling that something is going on with her husband and she manages to log into his phone to check his messages. She sees a back and forth conversation which seems to confirm that her husband is having an affair. Worst yet, the messages imply that the other woman is one of her best friends. As Kate seeks to identify the traitorous friend, it is clear that all of her friends have secrets to hide.

I have been in the mood for thrillers and this one did not disappoint. Once I got into the story, I could not put it down! We are primarily reading from Kate’s POV, hearing her suspicions, seeing her interactions with her friends and family. The author also gives us occasional chapters from the perspective of other characters, Kate’s friends, their husbands and the kids as well. It seems that almost everyone has something to hide and the author does a great job of dropping clues to redirect Kate’s suspicions and the readers’ as well.

This is very much a slow burn book for the first three-quarters or so. There is a lot of family drama and mystery going on which creates that slow build up to the last quarter where things really start to happen, ramping up the thriller elements. On top of the issues of what is going on with Kate’s wife, there are clearly secrets between the teens of their families and with the other women. The slow burn is done very well and it kept me entirely hooked throughout as the author takes the time to really delve into the different characters and potential suspects for everything that is going on.

I would highly recommend adding THE VACATION by T.M. Logan to your TBR!

title: What makes an Effective Teacher?
text:
10 Traits of Highly Effective Teachers by Elaine K. McEwan is well put together book, with lots of graphic organizers to clearly illustrate the ten traits. It concisely lists and explains the traits that make administrators and teachers effective. This book provides tools for teachers, administrators, and mentors to help others and themselves become more effective.
Principals and administrators will find ideas to help them improve instruction, become more able mentors, and motivate effective teachers. Teachers will find information and inspiration to define personal definitions of effective teaching. The book will give every teacher a renewed sense of mission and vision of what teaching can be.
McEwan's book divides the traits into three categories: personal traits, teaching traits, and knowledge traits. She introduces you to each trait through real-life examples, personal vignettes, and reflections of students, parents and educators. She provides many lists, questions, and exercises to empower teachers and nurture the ten traits.

title: This was one of the better books I’ve read so far this year
text:
This was one of the better books I’ve read so far this year. It was a nice surprise, being a debut novel about parenthood: it could have gone either way.

As the synopsis says, this is a character-driven story, and that’s what makes it so interesting and enjoyable. These are people that any toddler parent knows all too well. If you’ve ever been in a playgroup or online parenting forum/group, you can relate on some level to this book (albeit an extreme version of reality). It’s a look into modern parenting, in a yuppie world where everyone is following their own “parenting truth” and trying not to judge (though failing at doing so) others’. It is also a window into the complexities of “early-mid”adult life (if you can all it that)- relationships with others and with ourselves, and what is most important for each of us.

This book will make you smile, cringe and even think a little bit. What are the sacrifices we make for our families, for our loved ones, for our children? What are the personal costs? What wouldn’t we do to find some meaning behind the every day mundane? What is the difference between friendship and support?

I recommend it for any parent of young(ish) kids looking for an enjoyable summer read.

I don't usually write reviews, but I wanted to say something about this light set.

First and foremost, the lights are very nice for the set. It's bright, and are located in appropriate places. I like how the lighting at the bottom shines, and the interior light are nice and bright. The blue LEDS are very bright, it lights up my entire bedroom.

In regards to installation, the wiring can be tricky at some spots, but patience is the key. It took me about an hour, but I try not to rush things that are delicate and I'm not too familiar with.

The price of the lights are on the pricey side, almost 1/3 of the set. But if you are willing to pay for the actual set, then you can afford to pay for the lights.

Anyway, the one complaint I have with the lighting is the inability to disconnect the Ascent stage (TOP) and the Descent stage (BOTTOM) without easily removing the wires. It would have been nice to have quick disconnect legos to allow a person to remove the Ascent stage from the Descent stage, without ripping apart the whole set.

Yes, most people will probably just leave it alone. But I like to show the inside of the craft and let my kids handle the Ascent stage too.

But I would recommend the lights for anyone who likes to show off their legos.

title: Too many subplots.
text:
There are at least half-a-dozen subplots in this book, any of which could have (and should have) been a book unto itself. As it is, Pandora's Star is a disjointed narrative, flipping from one plot to another; not randomly, but annoyingly. At least two of the subplots are tedious enough that I ultimately just started skimming over those sections or skipping them entirely. Yeah, the author had a big story he wanted to tell, and it is an interesting story, but he didn't pull it off. Oh, and to end the book so bluntly just to make us have to buy his next one is just crass commercialism on his part.

That's not to say that there aren't great elements in this massive story. But they are few and too far between to ultimately provide a satisfying experience. My advice, regrettably, is not to buy this book. And even if you can borrow it for free, don't bother reading it. There are far better "space opera" authors out there.

title: Best new table-top or Skype-it role playing game!
text:
I have played this game both as a play tester Storyteller and Player for many years now, and I love it. Everyone (especially the stalwart Dungeons & Dragons players disappointed with the watered down D&D latest editions) loves the game system and basic premise: to become emperor at all costs (even at the expense of the other players). In that respect, it's like Celebrity Apprentice or Survivor in that the players work together but all are really scheming to outdo each other to eventually rise to such power as to become Emperor or Empress.

The whole game has an open spell system (this book [[ASIN:0692088644 The Adventurer's Rulebook: An Essential Component of the Immortal Empires Role-Playing Game for Mature Players]] ) where you create your own spells with a straightforward point system, 10 huge magical fighting arts (this book and the Storyteller's Codex) with 40 fighting art powers each, nonmagical Talents for fighters and thieves, politicians and assassins, and much more.

The system uses d10s only, and the opposed roll system is perfect. It allows the weaker characters a chance against the great characters, as in real life. Overall, it's a great game, in my humble opinion, and a great learning tool for math, vocabulary, and yes, even Latin!

To get a feel for the game, because it is costly (but it is well worth it as these are premium 8.5x11" full color laminate hard cover books), people should order the three available novels:

[[ASIN:1543132170 Mirror Motives: Immortal Empires of the Seventh Age (Immortal Empires Sextology) (Volume 1)]]
[[ASIN:1543141161 The Starborn War: Immortal Empires of the Seventh Age (Immortal Empires Sextology) (Volume 2)]]
[[ASIN:0692076018 Keeper of the Myst (Immortal Empires of the Seventh Age) (Volume 3)]]

as well as the other core rulebook for the game:
[[ASIN:0692088660 The Storyteller's Codex: An Essential Component of the Immortal Empires Role-Playing Game for Mature Players]]

title: Power of Darkness cut in half
text:
The first section reads like a Weird Mystery pulp telling of Dracula with some sexual innuendo from the Spicy pulps. It is surprising in many ways, not the least for prefiguring DRACULA AD 1972 with Dracula a cross between Ernst Stavros Blofield and a lewd version of the Godfather.

The novel also underplays the supernatural elements, explaining away some aspects of vampirism and crouching Dracula as the leader of a cult of half evolved vampire ape men.

Part two eschews any of the elements that make Stoker's novel a chilling peculiar masterpiece and quickly settles in as little more than a chapter by chapter outline introducing some minor new elements and prefiguring the ending of the play completely doing away with atmosphere and action.

Worth reading for the first half of the novel, but the latter section is little more than the Cliff Notes version of the classic.

title: This is an important book
text: First of all, I should say that I spent the last 12 years of my career working at a hospital as a Registered Respiratory Therapist, so when I received this book as a present from a friend I was excited to read it. However, after reading it, I was mystified by some of the critical reviews I found on Amazon. As an RT I spent a lot of time with patients who had breathing problems. This included patients with COPD/emphysema and asthma who struggled to breathe. The standard treatment for these conditions is a class of drugs called bronchodilators. Inhaling these drugs can save people who are unable to breathe, but especially the more chronic patients often don't respond as their bodies seem to become immune to the effects of the drugs over time. With these patients, I would often teach them some of the breathing techniques described in this book. Often I had great success in calming these patients (they're panicked because their damaged lungs make it difficult for them to breathe) and getting them to slow down their respiratory rate. I also worked in cardiopulmonary rehab with both patients who were recovering from heart attacks and pulmonary patients. When we exercised I noticed that most of them had forgotten about their diaphragms and were unable to isolated this critical pulmonary muscle during exercise. Mr. Nestor discusses this in the book. By the way, subsequent research based on the Framingham study does correlate decreased Vital Capacity (total lung volume) with increased cardiovascular risk. In any case, this book does not purport to be a medical textbook and many of the stories are anecdotal and not supported by volumes of medical double-blind studies, but I don't believe that it was the author's intent to propose breathing techniques as a way to cure diseases like scoliosis or ADHD, or as some sort of panacea for curing all illness. In fact, in the Epilogue he says this. But the book is a fascinating journey through 10+ years of the author's research into a much ignored topic. I believe that we can all benefit from practicing the techniques in this book. In short, I like his advice on the "perfect breath": Breathe in through your nose for about 5.5 seconds, then exhale for 5.5 seconds. Practice this for a few minutes. To your health!

text:
I've heard so much positive on these MH Creator Models, but never had the chance to find one at a reasonable price.

The statue itself is just STUNNING (it looks 100X better in real life as a side note) - Tigrex looks fierce and ready to attack in any moment. The amount of small brush detail that went into this thing is unbelievable, everything from its markings (stripes) to its tiny eye is spot on and has been skillfully painted - it's incredible to think it's merely plastic.

It's an extremely strong statue and base. In all honestly I think it would pretty difficult to accidentally break it with dropping it, although you might damage the paint job on it. It doesn't require major maintenence other than dusting it from time to time, but I would recommend storing it out of direct sunlight to help preserve the colors for years to come.

Without a doubt this is a must buy for any MH fan, especially those savvy of Tigrex. This looks fantastic on a display shelf and really is sharp/eye catching. As a die hard MH fan, I will definitely be keeping an eye out for the other Creator Models hoping for a good price again.

title: I love this book!
text:
I really enjoyed reading this book! Mona, the main character, is easy to relate to...and she has red hair! Being a ginger myself, I have a special affinity toward ginger characters (we're under represented)! My bias aside though, Holden's writing style really brings the characters to life. They are realistic...their lives aren't spectacular, they don't have these amazing careers or live in a mansion. They are normal people, living in an average house, complete with a crotchedy old neighbor! I love it. It was so easy to relate to their lives and picture them as my own neighbors or somebody I would be friends with. I was really touched by Mona's rediscovery of herself and her husband. There is a lot of laughter in Becoming Mona Lisa too...Mona and her husband have witty, cynical, comical personalities and I found myself laughing quite a bit. I also found myself feeling all gushy over the rekindling romance between husband and wife.

Holden does such an amazing job of describing the surroundings that I feel I could draw a picture of the Siggs home! I can picture the mean old codger that lives across the street, the bird infestation, the mannequins, even the Walmart that Mona works at. Throughout reading this book, I was reminded of the reasons I love my fiance and what brought us together. I don't know if Holden intended this...but it definitely reminded me not to take him or our relationship for granted. The book flows really well and I definitely found myself wanting to read more after I finished. So I'm really hoping there's a sequel to Becoming Mona Lisa, because I really wanna follow the next chapter in Mona's life...and I REALLY wanna know what's up with the room! I definitely strongly recommend this book.

text:
I got an affordable 2-pack of these plus another sleep mask to try. (I'd never used sleep masks before.) This one is good: very soft and light. It is pretty good about blocking light.

However, my other mask has contours so as not to touch your eyes: it is wonderful. This one: just pretty good. I can tell the difference for "sensory deprivation" that helps me forget about where I'm at and fall asleep easier and return to sleep faster at night when I wake up. This one is nice, but it is only pretty good compared to the one that doesn't put pressure on my eyes (Sleep Mask by Bedtime Bliss).

A warning: Don't tighten the mask too tight over your eyes! I wore this once recently during the day for a nap. I was worried about light, so I tightened the velcro a bit more than usual. I didn't think it was really tight at all, but I guess it was: when I woke up after an hour, my eyesight was blurry--even with my glasses on. Since strange things like this are sometimes normal if I wake during the wrong part of the sleep OR take a long nap too late in the day, I assumed it would pass. It took about an hour for the effects to wear off, and I was freaking out a bit the whole time. It wasn't until later that day when I remembered I had tightened the mask a lot more than I usually do. I'd hate to think what my eyes would feel like after a whole night if I had it tightened too much.

Katherine Center does it again! What You Wish For is a book I closely relate to. Sam is an elementary school librarian in Galveston who's amazing school is radically changed when their beloved principal dies and is replaced by Duncan, a no nonsense man who believes the school is shoddy in its security. Sam used to know Duncan, back when he was a fun-loving teacher, but can't understand why he's so different. Katherine Center always knows how to reach the right tone- the story is at turns sweet, eye-opening, soulful, tragic, and hopeful. She also gets the school politics exactly right- teachers know that a principal can make or break staff and student morale. It is refreshing to read a book that gets this right!

One recommendation- read Happiness for Beginners by Center first (or reread it if it's been awhile). This novel is completely a standalone book. Trust me, however- read it, not only because it's a fantastic book, but because it will add greatly to your enjoyment of What You Wish For.

title: Sweet, slow, sad
text:
Thin Wood Walls follows young Joe Hanada's family experiences during the time of WWII. After the bombing of Pearl Harbor, Joe's father is taken away by the FBI as a person of suspicion because he is a community leader. The rest of the family, including Joe's feisty grandmother and more feisty big brother Mike, are taken to Tule Lake Relocation Camp and must adjust to a new life while anxiously awaiting the return of the father.

Not much happens in the book, as camp life is boredom, waiting, hoping, but Joe tries to make do and make sense of what is happening while fearing what his big brother intends to do. The story is balanced, showing how not all white Americans were against the Japanese in the U.S. Some Japanese were very angry while many exhibited a sad stoicism. Perhaps what sets this book apart from other internment stories is that it is set in the Tule Lake camp, which was where troublemakers, the "no-no's" and those wanting to return to Japan were sent. This created a turbulent, sometimes dangerous atmosphere that other camps did not experience, at least not on that level. Thin Wood Walls delves into this in a manner suitable for middle-graders.

The book is a bit slow, but sweet, the writing rather plain despite the bits of haiku, but this will appeal to boys as well as girls and provide a thoughtful look at the sad facts of this long-hidden part of U.S. history. Expect a tear at the end, and be sure to read the Author's Notes.

[[ASIN:0939165538 Looking Like the Enemy: My Story of Imprisonment in Japanese American Internment Camps]] is also set in Tule Lake, but is a true story. A Young Reader's edition is coming out in Fall 2010.

title: Unoriginal and Uninspiring
text: If you happened upon this book by chance and are looking for some quantitative market insights, then do not be fooled by the books title. From a knowledge perspective the book is worthless. There are plenty of better books on investment theory. Paulos has "regressed to the mean" here. This work merely capitalises on his previous, better efforts. The book is tedious, and in many respects his arguments are fallacious. For example he postulates that if most investors became indexers then markets would cease to be efficient. This is not supported by economic theory, where the contrary holds. It only takes a small number of active investors to retain market efficiency. If you are in search of investment knowledge you will be well served by the author Ron Ross in "Unbeatable Markets". Paulos has not made a contribution here, he has merely compiled a collection of anecdotes from other authors and tried to spin it to make it look like his own. His humour didn't work for me either. If you insist you have to buy the book based on the balance of reader reviews let it be known that you have been warned.

title: Authentic characters make this a charming series starter
text:
I love how Austin's stories all knit together within the same small town community! You don't have to have read the other books in the series to enjoy each one individually, but by reading them all you get a fuller picture and more background on each of the characters. This start to the Bonfire Boys is a perfect example, taking minor characters from her other Love on Main series and putting them front and center.

Wild horses was a lot of fun, with city-girl-goes-country vibes. I loved Theron's inner battle and his relationship with his mother hits an unexpectedly heart-wrenching crux near the end. I didn't expect such a real moment in a romance novel, so it was a delightful surprise.

Skye is a satisfyingly believable character, with childhood damage and a lot of self-esteem issues. The way Austin describes her approach to and opinion of her paintings is incredibly accurate and gives the story an authenticity that many romance novels lack. Skye also gets her own personal wins that are unrelated to the romance, making you root for her even more. This (in addition to the sense of tight-knit small town community and over-protective family members) helps set a relatable stage full of players the reader can identify with.

Age gap usually isn't my thing, but this one worked fine for me. Skye is far more mature than her age. I enjoyed the self-conscious girl meets worshipping boy and city-vs-country tropes more. Theron has just the right amount of alpha-hole attitude and the steam is top notch. Looking forward to more in this series!

text:

The reason I chose this book is because reading it took me way back to when my mind was early in the stage of the exploration of literature. I owned this book as a child, and reading it gave me another small perspective on how our own life and time itself progresses.

Robert Munsch uses humour in alot of his books and this is another one of those cases. For example, at the end of this book, the child's father is suspended in the middle of the kitchen by his toe with a long rope.

Munsch also uses a form of anticipation to ensure that the child >wants< to turn to the next page. For example, most of the pages in this book have sentences that end like: "He looked in the kitchen, it was empty. He looked in the bathroom, it was empty. He looked in the garage and..."

Not only can I look at this book from the perspective of just an ordinary reader, but also as a child; the intended audience of this book. Because of this, I can say the Robert Munsch did a wonderful job of creating literature that will intrigue children for many future generations

title: Love it--a really fun read!
text:
I try really hard to not rehash the entire story or give a bunch of spoilers when I review a book, but it may be hard not to this time! I'll do my best, though. ;)

I received this book to rebiew from the Shut Up & Read group's Read It & Reap event. I have to say, I have been extremely fortunate in the books I've been given to review through them so far. There really haven't been any misses. :)

Anyway, about this book...

I admit it--halfway into the very first chapter I was convinced I was going to hate this book. Liora seemed like the typical, overly-angsty teenager often depicted in paranormal fantasy these days. I initially found her constant whiny and hating herself grating. All I can say is I'm so happy I read chapter 2!

Lucky kicks ass! There's really no other way to describe her. The demon half of Liora who takes over at night, separated from Liora by a curse, she is angry, obviously. And that anger is often turned toward Liora, her fully human side. She is also strong, practical, loyal to her friends, and more willing to look into herself and face the things that make her uncomfortable that she admits. And as time went by, I found Liora to be less annoying as she found her own strength and started to face her own inner "demons".

There are only a couple of things that prevented me from giving this book five stars. The first is that I felt like the romance between Keiran and Liora/Lucky felt too conveniently done to me. There didn't seem to be any build up to it at all. The second issue is that conversations sometimes felt stilted to me. While I appreciate that there was a distinct lack of inappropriate idioms throughout, the almost complete lack of contractions often made discussions feel too formal and unnatural.

This book had everything--romance, fear, growth, drama, excitement, sadness, and victory. It was a great story and I can't wait to read the next one!

title: Strong opening; a tiresome slog therafter
text: At least one reviewer on this page characterizes SIASL as "juvenile".  I'd have to say that pretty well sums up the greater part of this book.  In its day SIASL may have shone a light on the prevailing counter-cultural trends in American society.  And it may have been cutting edge sci-fi.  As such, it is perhaps of historical interest to those who might be interested.  To the casual reader, however, it's a pretty tiresome read.  The opening section, which deals with the protagonist's arrival on earth and initial adaptation thereto is quite interesting and well-paced.  The greater part of what remains, however, is given over to endless anthropological/religious historical musings of one sort or another, interlaced with endlessly banal descriptions of life in the Utopian commune our hero founds.  Much of this material fails either to titillate the reader's senses or to stimulate his/her intellect.  It reads like one long (LONG) masturbatory exercise on the author's part -- well-written, in fairness, but rather...juvenile.  As for the novel's ending: you'll spot it coming a mile away.  In the final analysis: SIASL is a creature of its times, ill-suited to our own.

title: Terrific light for video
text:
I have been using Neewer products for over 5 years. My first purchase was a cheap fluorescent ring light in early 2017 and have seen considerable improvement in both the variety and quality of products they offer while remaining reasonably priced. I have purchased several lights, a camera slider, tripod dolly, lens filters, etc. and everything has lived up to my expectations and I still use all of it. Nothing has ever broken or stopped working.

This light comes with the light unit, a mounting bracket to attach it to a light stand, a DC power converter, a power cord, a soft carrying case with plenty of foam padding, and an instruction manual.
It took only a couple of minutes to set up right out of the box. It was also easy to install the app on my phone and connect with the light via Bluetooth. The app allows the light to be controlled remotely and is intuitive and easy to use.

I tested this light this morning and plan on using it to light a video this evening. I had no problem using the Android app to control the brightness, color temperature, and effects. It can also be controlled manually via the knobs and buttons on the back of the unit. I tried using the Sony NP-F-style batteries (it holds 2) and the AC power. Each worked equally well though I would want more than one set of batteries if I were using them for a shoot. On the brightest setting, the light is quite bright and could be used as a key light. It can be dimmed for use as a fill or backlight. However, because it is a panel of lights, it cannot be used as a focused spotlight. The panel cover is a diffuser that softens the light considerably. It is built-in and not removable.

Overall I would say this is a terrific light and worth the price. Easily 5 stars.

I own 4 of these bottles of varying sizes. One of them is the BPA free version. I have never liked the rubber bite valve and have always taken them off right away. There is a rubber flap that covers the air intake hole that prevents water from getting out. The downside to this is it also prevents air from getting out when the bottle is just sitting. text: I purchased this for a long trip from VA to VT. I wanted to talk on the phone if needed, and do it hands free. This works great, as I had no Bluetooth in my 08 Nissan Altima. It only works through your car speakers when you have the radio on AUX input. This wasn't a problem on a long trip, as I had thousands of songs on my Samsung Galaxy S5 to listen to. I could listen to my music, skip songs when I wanted by pushing a button, and when a call came in all I had to do was say "answer" or push a button to accept the call. When the call ends, the music picks back up where it left off. To make a call, I could do it by voice (call Tina at home) or use the phone to dial it manually. It then stops the music and dials who you are calling. It doesn't work unless you have your car radio on AUX. You can't use the actual radio and use the SoundBot at the same time. It comes with a 12v plug (cigarette lighter plug) that has 3 USB outlets on it. One of those is used for the SoundBot, the other 2 can be used for GPS, phone charger, etc. Then there is a 3.5mm plug that goes to the AUX input on your radio. Your phone then connects wirelessly through Bluetooth to the SoundBot. I used my GPS on my phone, and the directions was heard through my car speakers over my music I was playing through my phone. I made and received many calls on my trip, and everybody said they heard me loud and clear. Great price on the SoundBot, and I loved it. I can't use it when listening to my local radio stations at home, but if I have it plugged in and connected, I can push the AUX button on my radio and use it then to talk. title: When Simple Faith is Simply Not Enough
text:
"Today, twenty-first century theology tends to make religion a belief based upon faith rather than a belief of faith based upon fact. History, science, and conflicting Scriptures are all too often dismissed when they conflict with accepted creeds or dogma. Most Judeo-Christians are taught there are certain areas of their religion they should not question, causing the phrase “it is a matter of faith” to be well-worn and overused.
Scripture encourages individuals to question their idea of God."
And question it she did!
For Jodell Onstott, like so many of us, simple faith was simply not enough. Unable to dismiss the passionate; yet, conflicting views of countless denominations… the seemingly endless interpretations of a single text… the bearing of historic facts and archeological discoveries… the consequence of scientific evidences… Jodell embarked upon a decade long mission to discover the not so simple truth. And though the title of the subsequent book, “YHVH Exists” may eliminate the suspense of her ultimate conclusion, Jodell’s journey is a masterpiece of well-organized testimonies and closely examined proofs. Leaving no stone unturned, her systematic examination of the data demonstrates a sincere desire to reach an objective opinion.
The long-awaited “YHVH Exists” is a thorough and fascinating study that will challenge your most hidden preconceptions, and, may well find itself on the more than one bestseller’s list in the process.
Well worth the wait!

title: High Adrenaline Thriller with quirks
text:
Music Notes is Manning Wolfe's second installation in the Texas Lady Lawyer series. It's a fast-paced, intense thriller with an eclectic cast, one of those stories that will keep you up so late at night you'll need extra coffee in the morning. Merit Bridges, the perky but powerful protagonist and her quirky team of paralegals find themselves, yet again, in opposition to a deliciously delusional villain intent on their demise.
When the rehabilitated rock guitar hero, Liam Nolan, is brutally murdered with his own guitar, Merit is not only responsible for his estate but feels morally obligated to help solve the crime. Enter Davey Ray Bell who claims to be Liam's love child. Though Davey seems lost and alone there may be some validity to his claim. Meanwhile, Liam's former manager, L A Baron, hopes to grab all the glory and the cash. When he fails to convince the legal authorities of his claim to the riches, he uses his vast resources to attempt to destroy Merit's career and reputation.
The writing is very visual and personal. Wolfe's characters are complex and for the most part driven by more than just material gain. Though the story is definitely dark, it's handled with a quirky humor and panache that brings this storyteller to the pinnacle of legal thriller authors. As an extra bonus, it's set in Austin Texas where the old hippie culture still clashes with the techno-boom of the early 21st century. Wolfe's Texas Lady Lawyer stories scream to be made into a Showtime summer miniseries featuring Reese Witherspoon and her ponytail as the protagonist. Check your local listings, but as always read the book first.

title: A little disappointed
text:
Michael Fallon's Dodgerland is an attempt to put the Dodger teams of 1977 and 1978 into the author's view of their cultural context.

When he writes about the way that new manager Tommy Lasorda prepared the team for the challenges of the '77 season, or the contentious Dodger clubhouse, he provides valuable insights. As a fan, these were some of my favorite Dodger teams of all time and maybe the best that I have ever seen play, even though they didn't win the World Series until 1981, so I found the "inside game" stuff interesting.

I could do with the liberal politics that the author espoused in the guise of a baseball book - as a lifelong Californian, I don't hold the author's favorable view of mayor Tom Bradley.

The author also makes the book a little autobiographical, choosing to write about his dad's hardware store and the author's role in the business. He also writes about a number of seemingly disjointed things, like skateboarding, author Tom Wolfe and other odds and ends.

He also makes some unforced errors - factual mistakes about the baseball stuff.

Overall interesting but not nearly as good as it could be.

title: Door Gym workout bar by Miniqi
text:
I ordered this product sold by 2 Guys and fulfilled by Amazon. It's definitely not "Iron Gym" brand. From what I can tell, it's a generic knockoff. The package says Door Gym and the company is listed as Miniqi.

The knockoff vibe is especially present when you put the full thing together because it's kinda crooked. It also doesn't respond well to being taken apart and reconstructed -- the plastic buffer bar can easily get stripped so really try to get things right on your first try!

But with that said, when it comes time to slip it into the doorway, it seems to work okay. Granted, I just put it together and used it for the first time today so I can't comment on its longevity. But it got the job done today.

Personally, if you're on the fence about buying this, I'd disregard all of the glowing 2008 reviews for the "Iron Gym" version of this product. This Door Gym is obviously not the same brand and I get the feeling that the Iron Gym was probably a bit sturdier.

Also, there was a random seed in my little nuts and bolts bag that came with the product. And an unrelated little metal piece fell out of the box when I opened it. It's definitely not part of the bar! I dunno what the deal is with that stuff but it definitely rounded out the whole knockoff experience.

title: Saved my daughter from a horrible fall

She passed concussion protocol right away and all mri’s and x-rays of her head/neck showed no brain trauma or skull fractures. She wound up walking away with a sore back and a broken arm and elbow. I can not emphasis enough having a quality helmet that fits your child. Please take the time to measure. My daughter is 10 years old, tall, but petite at only 62lbs. We measured and ordered her a size XS. It fit her perfectly. We did helmet checks with her instructor every lesson to make sure it was in good shape, fit well, and wasn’t compromised in any way. title: A Literary Spuge
text:
How many creative ways can one pose the vulgar? And we don't mean pose in the effete way, either. Perhaps this book will make you feel like Charles Manson playing the kazoo before an audience of irritable emperor penguins. Maybe.

It is hard not to take the printed "volume one" as anything but a threat, but it is a kindly one under the care of a good reader. Spitzer's short rocket-style blasts of the absurd, visceral, and tradition-baiting vulgarity makes for that kind of nostalgic reading many of us had as kids with the flashlight under the bed covers reading Mad Magazine. If you liked Spitzer's "Riding the Unit", you'll most definitely enjoy this more. In some ways, the irreal-ist quality of these shorts, wondrously masked by trademark obscenity, turns The Art of Fiction (1984) on its ear. Again, maybe.

There's simply not one bit of bathos in the whole lot, so hang on tight to your lawn furniture and have this book kicking around your cottage this summer.

This is contrary to a laser printer that has a higher initial cost and a toner that is moderately more expensive than ink cartridges but last infinitely longer. This has been my observation over the last 20 years as I've owned several inkjet and laser printers.

In current, "state-of-the-art" ball-point pens, the ink may not flow freely past the ball in the ball-point, so that the line skips, or it will write no line at all.  The Zebra pen used to be the gold-standard in ballpoint pen design, but something has been changed, so now, that is no longer true.  I have not had any problems with the Skillcraft Pen because this design is so simple and so basic.  Sometimes "new-and-improved" is not a good thing.  The Skillcraft Pen is a design that has worked in the past, and continues to work, so it is an excellent value for the cost.

title: Digital Babylon and Faithful Christians
text:
We live in a digital world, and one in which it seems Christians are swimming against the tide. Those who are coming to Christ in their youth within the digital age are often finding themselves lost in the sea. While following Jesus hasn't changed since Paul, it does look different from generation to generation. In an age of instant connection, limitless information, and constant entertainment, all filled with a value system that opposes God, "Faith for Exiles" asks the question of how we can create lasting disciples within this digital Babylon. In the digital age, "the goal of discipleship is to develop Jesus followers who are resiliently faithful in the face of cultural coercion and who live a vibrant life in the Spirit." David Kinnaman, president of @barnagroup, and @mattmatlock present 5 practices for Christians in the digital age.
•
1. Intimacy with Jesus to form resilient identity. Does Jesus bring you joy? Is worship a lifestyle? Is Scripture relevant to your life? Is your relationship with Jesus personal and intimate?
2. Develop muscles of cultural discernment. Is the Bible teaching at your church relevant to your life? Do you receive wisdom on how to live in a secular age? Is your worldview Christian?
3. Form meaningful, intergenerational friendships. Do you feel like you belong at church? IS someone encouraging you spiritually? Do you have personal close friends at church?
4.Train for vocational discipleship. Do you use your unique talents to honor God? Do you recognize God's unique calling on your life? Do you serve others in your church?
5. Engage in countercultural mission. Do you desire for others to see Jesus reflected in your life? Do you feel a responsibility to tell others about Jesus? Does the mission of the Church excite you?
•
This book seeks to create resilient individuals who cling to the truths of who they are in Christ, their purpose on earth, and the ways we serve and evangelize others. This book is packed front to back with research, statistics, diagrams, and charts. But the true fruit of the book comes in the theological insight and assessment of the next gen. The entire book is also gorgeously designed thanks to @chazrusso. **book graciously provided by Baker Books for an honest review

Model Information:

Manufacturer: GSA-A1175
Device name: ASMB012
Pack Lot Code: 012d
PCB Lot Code: 050d
Firmware Version: 646e
Hardware Revision: 2800
Cell Revision: 0000

Worth the price? Not really. One out of three might be a good batting average in baseball but not for purchased products. Take your chances, you might get lucky.

title: Excellent Zoom, Great Pics
text:
This camera replaced my previous Canon (3MP PowerShot S30). I will only buy Canon cameras, their picture quality is superb for a point-n-shoot. What sold me on the SX120IS was the 10X optical zoom.

The 10X optical zoom is spectacular! It gets wonderful pictures of our kids on the baseball field, and at concerts and shows. Pictures that 3X optical zoom could never do. Pictures from 100 ft look like you were standing only 15 ft away. I've had other parents ask me to take pictures of their kids, because they couldn't get close enough for a good shot. Yes, 10X is awesome.

The 10 megapixels are good, and the pictures are still great, but I am not impressed by pixel count. The overall picture quality is as good as my previous 3 MP canon, but not better. However, now the files are 3.3 times larger on my hard drive. Slower to open, slower to upload to web, and harder to email. The up-side to 10 MP is when pictures need cropped, there are still plenty of pixels remaining to make a good 8.5x11 print.

Do not be taken by the 3.0" LCD. Yes, it is big. But the resolution is not tight, so even though the LCD is bigger there aren't more pixels in it. And the menu fonts are big. I would have been just as happy with a 2.5" LCD with a tighter resolution.

All of the shooting modes are great, and easy to use. This camera has more "special" modes than my last camera, and they are nice. But one mode it does not have, and I miss it, is the panoramic stitch-assist mode. If you try to do a pano stitch with this camera, you'll have to guess at where you left off.

Overall this is a great camera. I would recommend it to anyone who wants beautiful pictures and a lot of optical zoom. Can't beat the price either.

title: Be careful what you ask for
text:
I got this book because I heard the author and her husband interviewed recently on NPR. Based on that, I thought "Wondering Who You Are" would be a uniquely uplifting story. I expected something along the lines of Jill Bolte Taylor's "My Stroke of Insight," which was a fascinating and inspiring first-hand account of a young woman's stroke and rehabilitation. For sure, this book did keep me on the edge of my seat - I couldn't put it down (as other reviewers have noted). And it did have some engaging parts, like the description of Richard's chaotic hospitalization, the couple's experience with a mediator over the legal settlement, and Lea's sexual exploration, among others. But I came away from the book feeling it was over-wrought and just plain sad. Here is a woman (the author) who actually leads a rich, surprising, adventure-filled life, but she just can't stop weeping over her lack of self-fulfillment. It's ironic that she spends so much of the book bemoaning the loss of her remarkable husband's pre-surgery personality, and yet while she had him that way, she was an alcoholic who preferred to be out partying rather than staying home with him and her children! Clearly she is transformed by her experience with him after he loses his personality, but she seems to find barely an ounce of delight in any of his rehabilitation successes or her own exploration of the wondrous possibilities life has to offer. Instead we hear too many times about her tears.

If nothing else, what this book teaches is - be careful what you ask for. If you long for unconditional love and acceptance, here is post-surgery Richard, able to offer these things in spades…. but it's creepy. Gurus like Byron Katie teach us the joy of living in the moment and questioning our personal narratives, but those approaches to self-transformation are only viable if we have a memory and a life story - as Richard does not.

title: Great Hold and Light Scent
text:
I have been using beard oil for a while, but recently, it was not making the cut and my beard was getting a little too scraggly for work. I decided to try beard balm to see if it might be able to provide some hold and tame down some of my loose hairs. I was worried that I would need a significant trim if I couldn't find a way to bring it all together, but since starting to use this balm daily, I have been able to let it grow without any thoughts about the professionalism. Below are a few comments I have to make on different aspects of this balm.

Size: This is a fairly large container. If you are looking for some size comparisons, I would say it is about the same diameter as a coffee cup and 3/4 of an inch deep. I have been using it daily for a few weeks now and still have well over 90% of the balm remaining.

Scent: As someone switching from beard oils with fairly strong scents, I initially thought this balm was scentless. I think this can be a positive or a negative depending on your preferences. If you are using a beard oil or cologne with a scent you love, this will not clash with it, but will give you the hold and conditioning you are looking for. On the other hand, if you are looking for a balm that will double as cologne, you'll probably want to buy a beard oil or some actual cologne to supplement what this will provide.

Strength: The hold is great! My beard is about an inch and a half to two inches, and this has provided the perfect amount of hold for me. It helps me to be able to do a little bit of shaping when I need to, but mostly allows my beard to be itself. It has also left my beard feeling less dry and looking a little bit healthier.

Overall, this is a great beard balm and I would recommend it to first time users or those who have tried many before. Also, I received this balm in exchange for an honest review.

title: Riddle of the Book
text:
It might seem surprising, but professional bibliographers (and I am one) invariably judge a book first by its publisher. In the case of this book, it is published by Springer, a prestigious European information conglomerate. This is important because the author of this book has notably airy qualifications as a "reporter." Digital Publishing allows everyone to be an author and anyone to be a publisher, and if you can tweet you can be a "reporter." Thus, it is truly important for readers to have some sort of crap detector in place. Unfortunately, the publisher test failed on this book.

This book has virtually no redeeming substance; Wikipedia says it better -- and cheaper. The author's writing style relies on a snotty-know-it-all approach, that is particularly irritating because he has no credentials. (As an example, he even manages to insult little Corvallis, Oregon as "a jerkwater town," even though the place is a pleasantly progressive college town). Essentially, the book is about grinding axes with political correctness uber alles.

Technically, the Kindle version of the book has way too many formatting errors and unpleasant (and unnecessary) decorative images. Why ebook publishers -- and especially wealthy publishers like Springer -- can't seem to at least look at their digital product in Kindle Previewer is a bigger riddle than Kennewick Man.

My take-away from this book is that I will no longer give Springer-Verlag an automatic pass. It's easier to lose respect than to earn it, mein Herren.

title: Look What I See
text:
This series entitled, "Look What I See! Where Can I Be?" which includes the previous titles that explored "the neighborhood", "the home", "my animal friends" and "visiting China", now examines "the synagogue" with mixed results. The publisher promotes the book as "exploring a week in Jewish family life", but that week constitutes a rather confused timeline for most adults familiar with Jewish rituals and traditions. The concept is one that is completely appropriate for very young children. An inquisitive toddler and her doll view items relating to Jewish rituals and then, with a turn of the page, we see her and her family photographed at the larger event. For instance, the text reads, "On Sunday, I fell asleep in my stroller. When I woke up, I saw a Kiddish cup." First we view the Kiddish cup in a clear photo, and then the toddler asks, "Where was I? By the Chuppah at a wedding." Within the wedding photo, clever toddlers will notice an apple and also the doll in his stroller. These photos and questions and answers are repeated 7 times for the days of the week and make for an appealing, structured format. However, this format does not work as well in a synagogue as it probably does for "exploring the neighborhood". Confusion abounds as we are led to believe that Rosh Hashana and Simchat Torah fall within the same week, or that apples are an integral part of every Jewish ritual. Confusion continues as the reader assumes the text to be the words of the toddler ("I fell asleep in my stroller"), but the photo then matches what the plastic doll is doing rather than the young girl. Also, the plastic doll, with a droopy, oversized blue kippah, is generally unappealing. Another issue involves the choice of photographs of both people and ritual objects. For example, the lulav is cut off, the dancers are blurry, and the "menorah" they chose to display is the stylized, artistic synagogue wall version, which is certainly not something a toddler would recognize from the home version. This book may work for some families comfortable with Reform traditions, but, in general, it needs to be revamped to appeal to its intended audience of Jewish families with small children.

Reviewed by Lisa Silverman

After all, it has been over a decade and perhaps a thousand books between the first time reading them and now, and when Jimmy the Hand swooped in, or Amos arrived, I broke out into a huge grin, fondly remembering them and delighted to hear about them again.

title: Another Gem
text: First off, knowing how to play the basic triads for the the 4 primary scales, major, harmonic major, harmonic minor and melodic minor in 4 string groups is a helpful instigator of original ideas. The inversions that skip strings sound even better. I like the inversions using the two forms on the first 5 strings, Vic prefers strings 6,4 and 3. Then you are given moveable roots to go along with these triad inversions that give mini alteration flavor. Next up are traditional 4 note chords and their inversions of which you must learn the most common alterations.  Vic then goes into areas of stacked triad and modal harmony which give the book it's 'advanced' rating, Fascinating stuff for sure. To come up with these ideas and relationships on your own would be very tuff unless you were an unrelenting genius with resources. He concludes with chord charts of various voicings that include open strings . There is tab but it's only used to clarify suggested fingerings. To get the most out of this book you would need to be a student of music but there's nothing stuffy or drawn out about the presentation. He points out useful scalic relationships for the modal chord forms and many musical examples of the concepts presented. It seems more essential theory than White Elephant Theory . I'd take this one with me to a desert island because many musical questions are answered pragmatically and unselfishlessly. With this and the Slonimsky interval bible, you could create brand new forms of music to entertain the crabs.

title: My kitten loved this cat litter but after a month had respiratory problems (silicosis symptoms)
text:
My kitten loved this cat litter but after several months, had respiratory problems (silicosis symptoms). When I took him to the vet to have him neutered, they couldn't proceed because they noticed he was short of breath and after listening to his lungs (lots of crackling short breaths & coughing occasionally), doing bloodwork (which was negative for any infection), an X-ray (which didn't show anything) & then giving me antibiotics because she knew something was wrong but couldn't find a reason for his respiratory problems. $375.00 dollars later, I brought home my sick kitten who still wasn't fixed.
Later that day it hit me that this fine, powder like liter might be the cause of his symptoms. After looking up how this fine silica sand could cause respiratory problems, I called my vet, explaining about the cat liter I was using and now his symptoms made sense to her. I too have been having similar respiratory problems (since I had a second litter box near my bed to make sure the kitten didn't have any accidents at night).
Although I had no problems when I only had my two adult cats using this litter, the kitten tended to play with the fine sand and was very thorough when covering offensive odors not just for himself but for the other two cats too. He often had pink sand on his nose, so it's not a big leap that some of it was getting into his lungs.
Just wanted to warn everyone that this litter is not a good choice for kittens. I've switched both cat boxes to fresh step premium crystals, it's a larger, pearl like bb which has no dust and is too big to be inhaled! Hope this helps others whose kittens are short of breath.

title: Good noise suppression and durability for a fantastic price
text:
I bought these after looking through various first- and third-party solutions for low-noise Mavic Pro props. I'm using them on an original Mavic Pro (not a Platinum) and I absolutely love them for 3 reasons:

1, they make a big difference in terms of the Mavic's sound output. I haven't done formal tests with a decibel meter, but it's obvious that the flights are significantly quieter with these props both indoors and out. I now tend to have some trouble hearing my Mavic once it's up to about 150-200ft even when directly overhead (though obviously quick altitude changes or movements change that). It's made it much less obtrusive than the original props. I haven't tried other brands and therefore can't compare to other manufacturers' low-noise props, but you'll definitely notice a big improvement over the stock blades.

2, their durability seems just as good as the original props'. I read several reviews of other low-noise props that complained that the gold tips were made of a softer, more easily deformed plastic. That isn't the case with these, as it's the same material along the entire length. That may make a slight difference when it comes to aerodynamics, but it means I don't have to worry about them when folding up the props (by the way, they fold up just fine despite their slightly larger size, as long as you're a little careful when unfolding the back legs and don't get the pairs intertwined). The paint scuffs relatively easily, but that's it. I've replaced one set after stupidly crashing into some scrubby branches, but even then there were only a few minor nicks and gouges that I probably could have gotten away still flying with, but at this price it's stupid not to just get another set.

3, obviously the price is amazing. These are half the price of all other manufacturers' props that I could find, and at $8 for a complete set it's really hard to argue with when you get such significant noise reduction. I can't imagine going back to anything else. I'd buy 2 sets just to have some spares.

title: Awesome!
text:
I'm kind of a cheapskate, so I was a little iffy on spending this much on a bird toy, especially with our parakeet cage filled with $1 plastic bird toys. Luckily, this purchase was definitely worth it! Our parakeets ignored it for a few days before cautiously approaching it, but after a week, they were going absolutely insane over it. I expected it to just be a bowling toy, but our parakeets found more ways to play with it than expected, which was a huge plus and something that we hadn't seen with a lot of the other toys, where they just chew and climb. They like chewing and pulling at the bowling pins, the chains holding the pins, the brown "railing" that the bowling ball is attached, to, and of course, the bowling ball itself. It took a little while longer for them to pull the top part of the stick on the ball to hit the pins, but they eventually did figure it out. The mirror was also a plus, since our keets LOVE mirrors. One of our parakeets likes sticking his head into the hole under the bar and moving everything with his face (he apparently likes doing this with a lot of things ;D)

The toy itself was very easy to install. The nut and screw mechanism keeps the toy securely attached to the cage. Our parakeets sometimes climb on top of the toy while playing, and it's fastened securely enough to support that. Build quality is also very good, and the toy is easy to clean.

Edit: We cleaned the cage and moved stuff around, and it looks like our parakeets didn't like the new location, as they ignored the toy for over 2 weeks. We changed the location again, and they're all over it again! So if you've had your toy in the cage for a while and your birds are used to its presence, but they're not playing with it, maybe moving it elsewhere could help!

title: This is a excellent read for new leaders.
text:
This is a story about Debbie Brewster. She is the new head of corporate client services.

Debbie's current situation is her team scores are the lowest in the company and she has to figure out how to improve them.

Debbie begins by trying to assess her situation on her own but then realizes she needs help.

Debbie discovers the companies mentorship program and signs up for it.
She gets Jeff as her mentor. Jeff is the companies president. They spend several weeks together. Jeff gives Debbie his secrets to becoming a successful leader. He teaches Debbie the SERVE model. He asks Debbie several direction questions about her self and team. Debbie's homework assignment is to answer those questions and bring the answers with her at their next meeting.

Serve stands for:
1)See the future - where are you going with your team

2)Engage others and develop them - Assign the right people to the right jobs and help them to smooth out their rough edges.

3)Reinvent Continuously - Continue to learn

4)Value Results and Relationships - Get results from those in the right position by being relationships.

5)Embody Values - Walk the talk. Be a role model for what you believe in and your team will follow.

As Debbie learns, understands and implements Jeff's teaching she begins to see excellent results.

This book is a quick but powerful read. I highly recommend to new leaders.

title: The Eternal Truth of the Simple Man
text:
Norwood Pratt has neither guile nor an education, but he possesses a comic wisdom that guides him from one nutty encounter to another. He is the man he is, regardless, slow to fight but ready to fight, honest, to a point, and rationalizing beyond that. He never internalizes, seldom jumps to conclusions, and just proceeds along the rightness of his course without question. He is a Faulknerian character distilled down to the basics, so unsophisticated he is hilariously honest.

Norwood is a fast-paced comedy of the simpleton winning out in the end because his sights are so low he can't lose, and Charles Portis' social commentary should not be missed, but if you do, the dialogue alone is worth the read. And if the characters in Norwood seem too silly to be real? Well, I recognized them more than I care to admit.

title: 3.5 Stars
text:
Story: I liked this story much more than the first book of the series (Need). I found that this plot line is better developed and more captivating. I wanted to keep reading and to know what was going to happen. And the end of the novel made me itch to read the third of the series. Unlike the first book (where I pretty much predicted everything that was going to happen), this book was different. It surprised me! Yay! That is an accomplishment in my eyes. One BIG surprise in particular really took me off guard. Ahhh! If you read this book, you will know what I'm talking about!

Characters: All the main characters are the same, likeable characters. Zara develops quite nicely in this book. And there is a new character, Astley, who I think I like. Astley is the new king pixie in town, but he claims to be different - he claims to be good. I like the way he is presented (just hope we can trust him!).

Writing: The writing quality is better in this book. It is still a bit weak, but it was able to captivate my interest. There are a few errors (or typos), but nothing really worth mentioning. I only mention the errors because there were soooo many in the first book. Big improvement here!

Uniqueness/Creativity: This book was also much better in the uniqueness and creativity department. Jones came up with unique and creative elements that I've never heard of before. So, yay! Good for her! And I didn't feel like I was reading Twilight this time!!

Overall: Overall, this book was good. It kept my interest so that I wanted to keep reading. I am itching to read the third book of the series! Can't wait to see what happens! Would I recommend this book? I would recommend it to anyone who really liked Twilight by Stephanie Meyer. If you are bothered by weak quality of writing, then I would suggest staying away. It's a good story, but the quality is a bit weak. Side note: I totally like how the king pixies need a queen in order to be strong(er) - I think it's awesome that women are needed by the men in this way! Hehe :)

title: A Christmas treasure
text:
This undiscovered gem of a book has been a Christmastime staple in my family since 1902. Owen Wister is best known for The Virginian, but he makes a major departure from that genre for this book. Set in 13th century England, The Dragon of Wantley is, in Wister's own words, a burlesque. He freely mixes charming anachronisms into his medieval setting. If possible, find the Fourth Edition, which includes several amusing additions, in which Wister takes on some of his literary critics.

I have now bought 5 copies of this book, as well as the one I inherited from my father. Buy it, treasure it and pass it along. Some day, I hope, the BBC will make a film version of it. Read it, and see if you agree that Brian Blessed was born to play the Lord of Wantley Manor.

title: Bill Peterson has depicted the Vietnam War as it was ...

I assess the value of this book through the eyes of an infantry platoon leader, having gone on countless air mobile operations during my own tour of duty in Vietnam. Most of the book is composed of his own letters home after having completed each operation. He was a crew member on active combat flights, often going into hot landing zones with incoming enemy fire threatening them and hitting their aircraft at times of insertion. WIAs and KIAs were not uncommon to him. As many of us over there, he was forced to experience much more than he should have. The book should be read by anyone who has had such experiences themselves or anyone contemplating such a venture in the military service. Bill Peterson is another of our veteran heroes, and a very effective author.

[[VIDEOID:85cb89701a2f395e248b9d8439d835ea]] This is a great drone for an incredible value. There are tons of features and functionality packed into this tiny drone which is the size of a smartphone when folded.

With these, I do need to take a little extra care mixing on my pallette, and also smooth out the cake of paint in the pan if using it on the brush directly. It handles a bit like a thicker type of paint because of the flake.

I like using them in skies or on water surfaces to add a little extra gleam and luminosity, so I tend to thin them out a good deal and.mix with other colors. They hold up well and blend well without losing their sparkly quality combined with other paints.

I also have the box of various blacks,and experimented mixing these with those on the page and ended up with profoundly 'velvety' luminousity. Like a photo of a velvet dress or curtain. Lovely. I will be buying more of these when they run out, which probably won't be anytime soon... They are large 2cm x 3 xm pans, about half full, for a total of 4-5 mm depthof driet paint. title: Mann's ambitious retelling of the Faust legend
text: Thomas Mann poured his considerable knowledge of music into this biography of fictional German composer Adrian Leverkuhn, whose musical career spans the first thirty years of the 20th century. The result is one of literature's most ambitious attempts to portray the art of music in words. At the same time, this is a self-portrait of the narrator. Writing from the perspective of 1944, like Mann himself he is a representative of an older, humanistic Germany, who looks on appalled as the Red Army marches ever closer to the German border. Hating the Nazi regime, he struggles with the fact of the national catastrophe that looms ever closer. The result is perhaps Mann's most complex novel, ironies within ironies, all contained in the story of an artist who makes a pact with the Devil (or does he? or does he imagine that he did?) in order to achieve transcendence in his art. The language is thick, the narrative moves slowly, sometimes at a snail's pace, but the complexity of the story offers rich rewards. Not for the faint of heart.

title: Where to begin...
text:
I have never before read a book where the author is so shamelessly self-promoting as Chris Brownfield. As another reviewer previously pointed out, his arrogance removes most (if not all) of his credibility, and makes this book very difficult to enjoy. For someone who was clearly not an outstanding JO (not by a long shot), he has way too much criticism and not enough respect for his fellow Navy submariners.

For a book titled "My Nuclear Family", Brownfield spends a lot of time talking about his IA in Iraq and his problems with the US government and the War on Terror. All organizations, particularly the US government has it's fair share of problems, however I hardly consider a sub JO an expert on politics or the intricacies of war. His claims that submarines are obsolete in today's Navy only further demonstrate his ignorance on the subjects.

I was led to read this book because I am quite familiar with the Navy's nuclear training pipeline and the job requirements of a submarine JO. As such, I was most interested in the first part of Brownfield's book which focuses on his time as a JO on the USS Hartford. It seems to me that Brownfield was a sub-standard officer at best, and is now a disgruntled ex-employee of the Navy who wanted to write a bitch-fest about how difficult his job had been while simultaneously making himself out to be the lone person deserving of respect in a profession he believes to be fallen.

I wouldn't recommend this book to anyone. The officers currently serving in our sub force are an important part of our national defense and are very deserving of our respect and gratitude, despite what Brownfield thinks.

title: Good price
text:
I read the reviews before I bought these. I honestly was not sure whether I'd be making a good purchase or not.

The price was right, and my VBS budget was rapidly shrinking- in fact, I decided to buy them out of pocket, because I thought it would be helpful.
Well, after 5 days of exploring, tumbling, game-playing, etc with kids ages 5-11, I'd say this was excellent value for my money. I only used the included cards for certain ones, since we color-coded the name tags for identifiability, but the card stock which is included, is of a really good quality. I have passed them on to our missions team, and they will use them!

Did they all make it thorough the 5 days? No. About 5 of the lanyards broke, but we just knot-tied them, and they were good to go. The rest made it through.

So if you are looking for an inexpensive option, that can withstand some rough and tumble, this is for you.

Edit: After I wrote this review, I spent an office day going through all my VBS supplies, and feel that I need to amend my review to reflect the following.
I had gone through the badges before, and they appeared to be in good shape. On closer examination, I found that almost all of them had been tied with a knot. So I guess that although as a whole, they lasted for the five days, and withstood, as I said, a LOT of rough and tumble, I have very few that I will in good conscience use next year. I will reuse some, but only as backups.

So, If you're not using them for children, and don't particularly care if you get to reuse them, it's still value for money.

I still feel that the value may have been lost to me, due to the fact that I will definitely have to buy more next year, I did save a significant amount during THIS budget period.

title: Great but not for me
text:
The writing in James Baldwin's 1953 Go Tell It on the Mountain is as good as writing gets, but this book wasn't for me. It's told through the filter of the Christian religion and while that may hold much sociological interest to many, none of it was new to me, though it is fascinating to think about it: A Middle Eastern religion, transformed in Europe, exported from there to America and then forced on unwilling slaves from Africa. But growing up in a fairly diverse East Coast city and having been raised going to church until I was no longer required to, the religious aspects of this book didn't interest me. The only part of it I found compelling was Part Three in which that element was least present, which the section that described the main character's origin story.
 If you're interested and don't know a lot about the influence of the church on American Blacks, this book—its working title was "Crying Holy"—is for you. Otherwise, you might be more interested in Baldwin's other works.

 On a bright, summer day, bright in her memory forever, she came into the store alone, wearing her best white summer dress and with her hair, newly straightened and curled at the ends, tied with a scarlet ribbon. She was going to a great church picnic with her aunt, and had come in to buy some lemons. She passed the owner of the store, who was a very fat man, sitting out on the sidewalk, fanning himself; he asked her, as she passed, if it was hot enough for her, and she said something and walked into the dark, heavy-smelling store, where flies buzzed and where Richard sat on the counter reading a book.
 She felt immediately guilty about having disturbed him, and muttered apologetically that she only wanted to buy some lemons. She expected him to get them for her in his sullen fashion and go back to his book, but he smiled and said:
 "Is that all you want? You better think now. You sure you ain't forgot nothing?"

title: A fun political satire and much more…
text:
The First Lady Escapes is obviously a satire of the current political atmosphere, but it is also an enjoyable, well thought-out story with a fun cast of characters. As I was reading the story, I found myself falling in love with several of them, especially Angel, the gay Mexican hairdresser, and Moon, a FLOTUS impersonator, and I was eagerly anticipating what would happen as each new chapter began. The short chapters are titled with a location and time to add to the fun so the reader can feel the excitement build as events unfold simultaneously at the White House and across the US and Mexico.

While the President is the focus of the political satire, FLOTUS and the characters who become part of her journey are well-developed and bring the story to life. The detailed descriptions of their surroundings and activities made me feel like I was escaping to Mexico with FLOTUS or part of the White House luxury being experienced for the first time by FLOTUS’ impersonator.

I picked up this book because I was intrigued by the premise and hoped for a few moments of escapism from the daily news. I got that and so much more. The author acknowledges the current political situation inspired her to write this satire, but beyond that initial premise, she created an entertaining story with well developed characters that evolve to show the people behind traditional stereotypes whether they are immigrants, paparazzi, or transgender. This is definitely not a read for supporters of the current administration. But for everyone else who has felt concern, frustration, or outrage as they read the latest news feeds, this book will put a smile on your face and even let you laugh out loud and be entertained for a few fun hours.

title: Sparks creativity, once you get past install problems
text:
The Digital Arts & Craft Studio from Fisher-Price is fun for the whole family (I think I used it more the first night than my 3 year old!), but you may be driven crazy by problems with the install process. Buyer beware if you are not willing to troubleshoot potential problems with buggy software.

In my case, I received the "Common Language Runtime Debugging error." If you do too, and your system meets the minimum requirements (and the firmware test, which comes with the software, works) then the problem is most likely your Microsoft .NET Framework installation.

I had 1.1 installed and it appears the program installs both a hotfix and .NET 2.0. To fix: uninstall everything (add/Remove programs). First, the Studio software, then NET 2.0, then the hotfix, and finally NET 1.1. Reboot, and reinstall from the CD. Everything should now work.

Took about an hour, but then we were up and running. Is it worth the money? My toddler is fascinated by the computer, and loves to draw, making this toy the perfect combination to keep her occupied (at least for a little while).

title: A Classic with a contemporary interpretation
text:
Not much needs to be said here about the story of this truly perennial classic. The War of the Worlds (1898) is the account of Martians invading earth, attacking and ruining London. What happens to the rest of earth and mankind is not resolved till the very end. Although this novel was seen as the start of modern science fiction, it had also a deeper meaning of fighting tyrannies and the occurrence of mass-hysteria.

This deeper meaning was clearly shown when Orson Wells broadcast in 1938 an extremely believable radio dramatization. Listeners thought that Martians were actually attacking and in panic they left their homes trying to escape this terrifying experience. It is interesting to note that that broadcast happened at the eve of World War II.

Now in 2005, a new movie adaption has just been released by Steven Spielberg and starring Tom Cruise. While I'll leave it to movie critics to evaluate that movie, it has already received wide acclaim for its special effects. Something else interesting to note is that in the early scenes of the attack by the Martians, the children of the character played by Cruise question whether these are attacks by "terrorists". In an era where we are sandwiched in time by 9/11, the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, and further terrorist attacks in Bali, Istanbul, Madrid and London, the world seems again in the grip of fear, of wars and of mass-hysteria. One could wonder if The War of the Worlds in 2005 again will create or foresee further scares in the world.

What makes this edition of The War of the Worlds so worthwhile is not just the inclusion of the classic illustrations by Henrique Alvin Correa, but also the introduction by Robert Bartholomew. Bartholomew is a leading expert on panic attacks, media manipulation and mass delusion, and he puts this book in historical and contemporary context. He tries to answer why this book has "created" such a scare in 1898, in 1938 and maybe again in 2005, or is the scare in all of us us calling this book into everlasting existence? I rate this edition 4 stars, and just wished that the publisher had considered releasing a hard cover edition.

title: Panasonic goes out of its way to avoid rewarding loyalty
text:
First, my refurbished units work just fine - no problems there, at least not so far.

I've had earlier versions of these Panasonic phones, and they work well. Compared to earlier versions, there was one pleasant surprise and two unpleasant ones.

The good, compared to earlier versions - the display is easy to see. I got this set for my parents, so that they could have phones all over the house, and the display makes them easy to use.

The bad - first, they took away the intercom button. Instead of just pushing the intercom button and then selecting which handset to call, you have to select menu, then scroll down several steps, then select intercom, and then scroll down to pick the handset to call. The steps are slow - every time, the menu takes a noticeable amount of time to appear, as does the list of handsets. So, the entire process is at least 3 times as long and cumbersome as before. They took an easy feature and made it painful.

Second, every single time Panasonic comes out with a new version of these phones, they go out of their way to make sure that loyal, repeat customers can't use the old bases to charge the new handsets. Keeping the base design the same would reward loyalty, but instead Panasonic literally goes to special effort to make sure that repeat customers are screwed on this. For that reason alone, I'll go out of my way to avoid buying anything whatsoever from Panasonic in the future.
