title: A brilliant but flawed man
text:
After watching the film, "Finding Neverland", I was curious to learn more about the fates of the 5 boys orphaned in the story. Although Barrie did not gain custody of the boys, he did maintain a strong presence in their lifes. In fact, he did much more than just keep an eye on them over the years. He showered them with gifts; traveled with them; and of course, financially helped them. He seemed particularly obsessed with the older boy, George. Barrie loved to photograph all of the boys and some of the photos included in this book show the children naked. Was Barrie a pedophile of sorts? None of the boys ever accused him of such. And Barrie's love and concern for the boys did not end when they became men who were tall enough to tower over the diminutive playwright.

This is a comprehensive look at Barrie's life without passing any judgement. That is left to the reader. And after reading this book, I have to say that I'm STILL unable to figure the man out. He is an enigma. There are tons of photographs - one or two on just about every page. Original correspondence and notes from Barrie's diary/journals add further insight. A fascinating, and sometimes tragic look back in time.

title: Will to Power
text:
Reading Mr. Simmons' "Kiss and Make-Up," even the most churlish reader cannot but immediately grasp that he is the Baudelaire of his generation. Though never so despairing as his 19th century counterpart, Simmons nonetheless explores and exposes with refreshing candor the darkest impulses of the human spirit while affirming the life force of pure carnality.
While the less perceptive observer may dismiss Simmons' work as masturbatory egoism, it instead reveals the realization of Nietzsche's Ubermensch. Maligned and misunderstood, the true Nietzschean "Over-Man" rejects conventional behavioral norms and aspires to self-authentication, self-affirmation. This man is Gene Simmons - Bohemian visionary, fearless poet, nimble entrepreneur, and voracious lover of life and women.
Part Byronic hero and part Le Petomaine, Simmons, in "Kiss and Make-Up," offers the reader a glimpse of the redemptive power of debauchery.

title: Safe and Extends the Life of the Port
text:
Have you ever gotten the feeling that USB-C ports are made a little too flimsy, especially on laptops? How they wiggle just a little too much? How it seems easy to scratch the center part with the metal plug if not inserting the connector just so? Well I have and since only 1 is included on my laptop, I wanted to protect it. That's why I ordered these adapters.

These are two part adapters, one piece can be left connected to the laptop and only protrudes a few millimeters out (less than my mouse receiver). The other piece can take the damage of plugging/unplugging USB devices in and out of it saving my one and only USB-C port from the damage.
The magnets on these are very strong and requires more than a little tug to disconnect them. One concern I had was "Would I get shocked by the part that remains in the laptop?" I am happy to report the electrical connectors are recessed into the connector itself while the part that disconnects has the protruding plug. In other words, the part I leave in my laptop is the female part of the adapter. So, no accidental electrical shocks.

title: Very good performance at a nice prices.
text:
The scale was relatively cheap so I was concerned about its precision and accuracy, so I weight 6 coins to see if the claims could be verified. The test showed the Standard Deviation of the measurements was less that one milligram per gram. As to the accuracy the standard provided was not much use as it was probably used to do the initial calibration of the scale, but it was useful in assessing the repeatability, which was very good. I got 100 grams each time I weighted it. To get an idea about the accuracy I used the coins, which when new have very consistent weights. The coin test showed about 0.25% deviation from what clean new coins should have weighed. As the coins were neither new or clean, in my opinion, this is very good for a scale of this price. As I am going to use the scale to titrate my medicines, the accuracy and repeatability are very important to me. These scales appear to be way within my criteria. The scale appears to be well made, but at this time I have no idea how reliable it is.

Now the bad news: parts of the protective shielding were not included in the package. The vendor promised to send me the missing parts but they have not arrived yet. I’ll update this review in two weeks or so with an assessment of the vendors performance. Update: they arrived!

I have found the scale is repeatable, but is does not respond to a small load change. Say 4 mg plus or minus. The work around is to put pressure on the scale for a second or so and it will adjust the reading correctly. This second delay is a little irritating but it probably deals with air currents and vibrations constantly changing the readings and the microprocessor spending time averaging the readings. I have been titrating one of my meds to 1.375 mg dose, which works out to 60 mg of the ground up tablets and I was able keep 37 doses all with in +/- 1.5%

This is poetry with room to move, to reach out tendrils and wind its way around the profane and the erotic, Mongoose bikes, ballot boxes, umbrellas, Soviet kitchenettes, news anchors, and the miasma of Americana on the precipice of an apocalypse. LaFemina rejects gratuitous allusion in favor of contemplation of the commonplace, elevating the thing-ness of things, refusing to surrender to the ordinary. There is a leitmotif that I'm not sure was a conscious choice of the poet, but it is delightful all the same: Klee's cat, Schrodinger's cat, his cat, a lover's cat, raining cats, and an apophatic mention of Eliot's cats. And his take on the uncertainty principle? Divine.

text: My wife and I took these out for the first time this weekend.  I only configured it for rider/passenger because all the modes it supports struck me just a little too busy at first. At first we tried opening a connection only when we wanted to talk.  It would connect so I could hear her, or she could hear me but not both.  We'd pull over and fiddle with it (on/off, connect/disconnect) then we'd get it working, so off we'd go.  But then next time we wanted to connect it would fail again.  After about thee times we decided to leave it open/connected.  Problem with that is it's transmitting engine noise and everything else the whole time.  Modulating the volume below about 3/4 results in faint garbled transmissions, not simple volume reduction.  The beep tones it issues, on/off, connect/disconnect, etc. are violently loud at any volume setting.  On my VTX1300 (v-twin) anything above 40 mph is too loud to practically use the unit even at max volume.  Now, I'm not blaming the unit for the noisy bike, but this is a factor to consider if you're buying.  You'll notice I still rated it 4 of 5 because it does what it claims and the overall convenience, feature set and price point beats anything else out there.  I also still hope to resolve the connection issue; I'm going to review the manual and play with it some more on the chance that I missed something with the operation - I'll update the review if I find anything.

text:
The assembly diagram for this toy is an absolute mess. The box says it is for ages 3+, but it took three adults to assemble this toy following the directions enclosed in the package. The photos are very small, the product being assembled is rotated into different positions in some of the photos, and the colors of the pieces switch from photo to photo which makes it very difficult to orient the towers properly during assembly.

My five year old really enjoyed the toy once assembled, though my three year old struggled mightily with the marble releases at the top of the towers. The recommended age is far too low, and while the box says it is fun for babies, I would not want my two year old anywhere near this thing. The marbles are about half the size of your typical marble, which makes them rather dangerous for little ones. Incidentally, the marbles are proportional to the rest of the marble run, as it was much smaller when assembled than expected. It would be more appropriately named a miniature marble run.

The toy itself is STEM friendly, teaching kids cause and effect, gravity, and more, though I cannot recommend this toy due to the poor assembly instructions, safety concerns, and poor quality of the materials. This would be fine for an older kid (8-10 years old), but at that age, I don't believe they would find it to be interesting enough to be a worthy investment.

title: Not compatible with my HP printer
text:
2/20/22 update: Today I needed to replace two cartridges, so I used two that had been provided to me by the vendor after my initial 1-star review of this product in which I noted that the cartridges were not compatible with my HP printer. The replacement cartridges worked just fine, so I have updated my review to 5-stars. Kudos to the vendor for addressing my issue. Please read below for prior reviews and additional background.

2/8/22 update: Within a day of my leaving the 1-star review, below, the vendor contacted me offering a /replacement or a refund. They said that their cartridges had "gone through a upgrade just because of t/he firmware update". That statement was not totally clear to me, but I took it to mean that the printers had a firmware update and that they had upgraded these cartridges so that they'd be compatible. I appreciated the offer of replacement or refund since I was out of the return period, and decided to give them another chance. So....I took the replacement which arrived today (only 3 days after they initially contacted me). My printer is not currently in need of any cartridges, but when it is, I will try the replacements and update my review accordingly. In the meantime, I've upgraded my review from 1 start to 3, for their attempt to make it right. Can't give a higher rating until I confirm whether the cartridges work.

Original Review: Even though the product description listed my HP printer as one that these cartridges would work in, and even though they appeared to be a match and were easy to install in the printer, they were not compatible. The printer indicated it had detected a non-HP chip, and the cartridge was blocked. This prevented the printer from doing any printing/copying. Unfortunately, since I buy my cartridges in advance, so that I'm never caught without ink, by the time I discovered this issue, I was beyond the refund period, so I had to eat the $70+ cost (including tax). I was pretty surprised by this....these cartridges had good ratings, and I ALWAYS buy off-brand cartridges and I rarely have problems. Maybe I just got a bad batch, but figured I should post this review just in case it's becoming a trend for these.

title: Easy Vegetable Dishes for Even Your Picky Eater
text:
From the Book's description:

Everyone knows that vegetables are healthy and a necessary part of our daily diet. But not everyone knows just how delicious they can be. Sensational Vegetable Recipes shows you how to make great main meals from vegetables, as well as side dishes and delectable snacks. There's also a chapter on quick one-step ways to cook ten of the most popular vegetables. The clear step-by-step photographs guide you through each of the recipes, clearly explaining techniques that may be new to you. And there is practical advice on buying, storing and preparing vegetables, and ideas to let you take advantage of the great range of fresh and packaged produce available in markets today.

My Review:

I bought this book at my local Borders store in the bargain/clearance section years ago. What caught my attention was the bright colored vegetable dishes and the claim of step-by-step. Since then, I"ve made many of the recipes, including a family favorite "Savory Fennel Crumble", easy side dishes such as "Warm tomato and herb salad", "Asparagus and snow pea salad", Main dishes like "Vegetable lasagna", "Vegetable Pie" and so on. I've even tried the sections on the most popular vegetables, carrots, onions and so on.

The recipes truly are easy, step-by-step, for anyone, from the novice home cook to the tried and true professional chef. Falling somewhere in between, I found the recipes easy, delicious and crowd-pleasing. I've taken them to pot-luck dinners where everyone wants to know the recipe! They are made with common, every day ingredients, easily found in your hometown grocery store, the steps are not complicated. You may even win over your family's picky eater!

I would recommend this vegetable cookbook to anyone looking for something fresh for the family dinner. Even though it is no longer in print, there should be copies floating around the internet and used book stores. Easily five stars.

title: Something of a Find
text:
I'm very happy with this cart, and two reasons stand out: its sturdiness and its size.

It's a very clever design, and the parts are of high quality. The result is a rigid structure that's perfect for applications like mine: support for a wide-carriage "pro" printer that can be placed on the top shelf without the somewhat massive printhead action causing side-to-side sway.

The size is a difficult one to find elsewhere. In my case I needed to replace a cheap TV cart made of low-density fiberboard and formica. I was using it to support not only the aforementoned wide printer on top but also a laser printer and scanner on the lower shelf. Any replacement would have to be almost the same size because of my office setup. I was ready to give up -- most shelving/carts like these are dimensioned in multiples of 12 inches -- but then I found this guy (the 16x28). Perfect! A little taller than the crumbling TV cart, but that's OK. I gained a third shelf for supplies that previously lived on the carpet under the cart.

One problem (for me): Carts like these have no sides onto which you can stick things -- in my case USB hubs. The solution was fairly simple: pegboard material cut to size, held in place with toggle bolts (with shortened screws).

One caution: unlike wood shelf units, which typically have uniform shelf width front to back, carts like these have tubing at the four corners that you might need to take into account. If your printer, for example, is a tight fit on one of the lower shelves, it might fit fine and work fine but not allow you to pull out the paper supply drawer if you can't skooch it over. The inner post-clearing distances for the shelves in this case is about 25.5 inches (left-to-right as pictured) and about 13.5 inches (front-to-back as pictured).

Regarding ease of assembly... Yes, the instructions are terse, but it's not rocket science. If you have a third-grader in the house, you should be fine.

All in all, a very satisfactory purchase and a good value.

title: Excellent narrative but questionable claims
text:
This is an excellent narrative history of contributors, ideas, movements, and events in German culture. Peter Watson communicates his encyclopaedic knowledge very readably. He summarises major thinkers and cultural movements concisely, but rigorously, with a great gift for succinct meaningful précis.

However, Watson’s claim that the extent of the German contribution to modernity is unique (eg page 828 on ‘The First XI of Modern History’ which includes Mendel!), is unsustainable. Roy Porter claims otherwise in his ‘Enlightenment: Britain and the Creation of the Modern World’ as does Sudhir Hazareesingh in ‘How the French Think’. It is in any case a claim which lends support to the objectionable idea of German superiority. Renaissance and Enlightenment were pan-European projects.

Watson’s interesting thesis is that Pietism, Bildung and Innerlichkeit account for the German genius, but he does not show how these qualities of individual worth and spirituality fit with a strong tendency to communal obedience in German culture. He does however show how nationalism was initially a liberal idea challenging the old illiberal autocratic feudal German states.

Watson does not cover the major contribution of church, particularly in post-war German society. The West German Protestant church established the bi-annual ‘Kirchentag’ movement dedicated to persuade the German Christian to follow individual conscience rather than state dictat, and to include the outsider. The East German church hosted the political reform movement that led to ‘die Wende’, although the East’s DDR resisted acknowledgement of Holocaust guilt for too long.

Watson has provided a mine of data for a fuller debate on the causal factors, the nature, and the extent of the German contribution.

The colors are vibrant, and the pieces are thick enough to take some minor abuse. The photo on the box provides a guide, and the pieces are marked on the back with letters that allow you to "group" them together to make placement a little easier.

I definitely enjoyed putting this one together, and it's sparked my interest in trying more puzzles at home. After all, my next cruise isn't for another 4 months!

For me, 18 bucks well spend...and the time it will same me is more important.

With this you can plan a meal. Just start the chimney about 15 minutes before you want to put the meat on. My brother-in-law saw a similar product at Walmart. title: A captivatingly beautiful story!
text:
Tethered Angel, by T.M. Brown, is a captivatingly beautiful story, one that captures the reader like a gentle wind and takes them on a journey which must be seen to its end.
Set in the 1950’s and the burgeoning sixties, Tethered Angel follows Angel, the center of this story, an African-American teenage girl who is struggling to find her identity in a culture which is quickly changing, during an era of racism against blacks and the growing equal-rights movement under the leadership of Martin Luther King. Angel finds herself drawn away from her impoverished lifestyle by the taunts and serpentine appeals offered to her by a rich white woman. The woman convinces Angel, more by force than by reason, to travel with her to Europe, to see the world, leaving her mother behind with just a note. The story which ensues embraces the world of a young black girl at a time when racism is still pungent and violent, where people like her are treated as second-rate human beings, and where she learns to discover her strengths. Throughout the story, Angel converses with those she has lost, the dead, but her visitations from the lost and gone are more like guiding spirits, helping her through difficult times. As she grows and as her independent mind sees another road leading away from a world of bigotry and hate, Angel decides she must make it back to her mother, even years later, in spite of her new state of slavery to the rich white woman. The question is how? This is a story about courage, values, belief in oneself, and the persistence often necessary in life to climb one’s mountain. A very good read.

title: Too many contradictions - sometimes on adjoining pages
text:
I wanted to like this book, despite having read O'Reilly's "Killing Patton" which contained a very thin conspiracy theory about Patton's death. "Legends and Lies" purports to be a history book but is filled with inconsistencies and inaccuracies.

For example, on page 5, the book states that "Daniel Boone was born in Pennsylvania in 1734, the sixth child of ...". Yet on page 6, in a photo apparently depicting an unidentified stone house, the cut says "... Daniel Boone was the seventh of twelve children." Which is it?

On page 67, the narrative talks about Kit Carson being attacked by a band of Kiowa Indians on November 25, 1864. "Within hours, about fourteen hundred warriors attacked. It was similar to the situation in which General Custer would find himself a few months later." But 'Custer's Last Stand' occurred on June 25, 1876, nearly twelve YEARS later, not 'a few months.'

Also on page 67, "... while the Navajos, after signing a treaty in 1868 with General Sherman, were moved to a portion of their traditional lands, where they have remained." But on the photo on the facing page, the cutline says the Navajos "...settled peacefully on this land, as negotiated by (Kit) Carson." But in 1868, Carson was in Colorado, either dead or dying, according to the same chapter.

While any history book might understandably contain discrepencies, when compared to other history books, it should not contradict itself, especially on adjoining pages. For that reason, I stopped reading this book about half-way through and consider it a waste of money.

As the stars say, I really liked this book. This does not, however, mean it was without its problems.

Issue #1: Stud-in-residence (the police chief) calls ex-stud (contractor/carpenter) "Bob the Builder" - more than once. Both are (understandably) concerned for the MC's safety. When they are trying to talk her into staying safe, they say things like "don't be such a Nancy Drew" or "you're running off like Dora the Explorer".

Seriously? Two adult macho males referring to children's TV programming? I would have let Bob the Builder pass (though it twanged something in my head), but Nancy Drew and Dora the Explorer?

Issue #2: In a small section the author's editor apparently went on break. In the space of just a few pages, I read "peaked into the refrigerator", "share's my blood" and "for Cinnamon and I". All three of these are glaring errors that shouldn't have existed had the writer paid attention through middle school English/Grammar classes.

Having griped about those two issues, I must reiterate that I really liked the book. It had a slight comic book feel to it - A good slice of humor, quirky supporting characters, some adventure and danger, and an ending that I didn't figure out until it was time to do so.

title: Sarah has a beautiful way with words
text:
The 411 by Maria:
I received this book right before Mother's Day. It is absolutely incredible. It is one perfect, powerful poem. A poem made into a book for mother's to give daughters and friends to give each other.

Having a daughter for me, was on my bucket list. I knew I didn't have much say in the matter and prayed for Goddess as hard as I could without going overboard afraid that if I begged too hard, God would feel it was unfair and unwarranted.

What Sarah Kay does is takes everything I have ever felt or thought about my daughter and put it into words. Every girl should have a copy of this book. They should read it and re-read it because Sarah speaks the truth. Life will hit you in the face and wait for you to get back up so it can kick you in the stomach. This is a healthy dose of reality but written in a poetic, joyful way, truly beautiful way.

Apologize when you've done something wrong. .
But don't you ever apologize for the way your eyes refuse
to stop shining; your voice is small,

title: More Complex Than Expected, Still About Maids
text:
I demoed this game at release, and was at first a bit daunted at the amount of apparent setup. It's not that there's a lot of setup, but if you don't sort the cards after each use, you're going to spend the first twenty minutes before playing getting them all sorted then. This seems like a 'well duh' type of comment, but remember this is a game that appeals to two types of people: card gamers (who are used to scoop and box) and those moe gamers (who aren't going to want to wait to look at the pictures). If you are planned on introducing new gamers to Tanto Cuore, I greatly recommend that you have the game setup a head of time so you can dive right into it.

Game wise, it's not the deepest strategy in the world, but you can definitely play a few interesting tricks if you really put effort into it. This again can come as a shock to some gamers. Don't be deceived: It's the maids that are attracting players, and the idea that there could be actual gameplay to go with those maids throws a number of gamers off. Drake, an artist friend, was originally in it for the breasts; when he realized he was starting to lose, all the imagery faded out of his thoughts and he could have been playing with text-only cards.

It's very much a game that sells based on the images, obviously. However, if you get past the snorts and giggles, you can find an actually fun game with just enough strategy to play. Just keep it on a high shelf if you have young ones about.

title: The Connected Educator: Learning and Leading in a Digital Age
text:
I don't lightly rate books "I love it", but in The Connected Educator, Sheryl Nussbaum-Beach and Lani Ritter Hall practice the connected learning and leading of which they speak.

Prior to reading this book, I had been becoming a connected educator for almost two years. Then I found Sheryl and Lani hosting this book in a book study for Connected Educator Month, 2012. I joined in the study as much as I was able, since it was the start of a new school year, but watching them at work connecting and learning with those in the community cemented the learning for me.

The Connected Educator: Learning and Leading in a Digital Age is a great book for wherever you are in digital age learning. Chapter 5 is a mini encyclopedia the basic web tools you should use and why to use them. In addition, I believe it is imperative for present and future principals to read Chapter 8, "Transforming Leadership for a Connected World."

Overall, I understood more deeply the philosophy of learning and leadership behind much of what I was learning to do. Now I am more committed than ever to learning and leading in the digital age.

Thanks, Sheryl and Lani.

title: Colored natural, kinky hair
text:
I have bleached and colored natural, kinky hair. This is the first time I've ever colored my hair and I made sure to do my research on colored hair care, which includes protein treatments. Well, months had gone by and I still hadn't done a protein treatment. Madness, right? Eventually, the dyed parts (especially the ends) started to feel rough and dry.The ends were also knotting like crazy! I remembered a YouTube video I watched about hydrolyzed wheat protein. I ordered that and a pair of hair shears (prepared to do some clipping, which I had also been neglecting). I heard that you should expect to see results after the first use, but I was blown away! First, I cleansed my hair with shampoo. I didn't measure how much of the treatment I used but I mixed it in with my regular, wash out conditioner. After coating my hair in it, I covered my hair with a plastic cap then sat with my conditioning heat cap on my head for about 15 minutes.
My hair in general, not only the dyed area, feels softer and the colored ends feel smooth and manageable again. Also, waaaaay less knotting. After washing my hair, I put it in twists to dry. 2 days later I pulled out the twists to get a lovely, voluminous twist-out. Unfortunately, I didn't get the shears but Amazon promptly refunded me and I plan to reorder them shortly. I'm ashamed to say its been months since my ends have been clipped (which just compounded the problem) and I plan to use my protein treatment around once a month and trim when needed.

title: Noise Reduction Techniques
text:
There is a specific topic in this book that I have not seem covered in any of the 25+ book that I have on electromagnetic phenomena. The topic is the shield cut-off frequency of a coaxial cable. Common-mode currents at low frequencies (below a few hundred hertz) cause noise problems with coaxial cables, but signals above tens of kilohertz do not. This is vital data which is apparently not explained in many text books. For me, this topic justifies the cost of the text. Having said that, I am annoyed because the book is quite expensive relative to other books of its size and age. The point is that you have to buy it, but it is expensive to do so.
Even an advanced designer will benefit from this book, although you, like me, won't necessarily want to read all of it. It is sufficient to pick and choose areas of particular interest. The less advanced designer would clearly benefit more and the book would therefore represent better value for them. Given a choice between this one and Morrison's Grounding and Shielding Techniques in Instrumentation, pick this one. This one is more technically accurate and useful.

title: Not Recommended for Screenwriters
text:
I wouldn't recommend this resource for aspiring screenwriters. I had hoped that this book might offer some off-beat advice, but instead it quoted Goldman's classic Adventures in the Screen Trade and made endless references to film examples without much explanation.

In order to get much out of it, I think you have to be extremely well-versed in the films they are referencing, some of which are rightfully obscure (given the aim of the book), some of which are not great examples, and many of which are dated (many come from the 90s, presumably leftover from the original edition). While the authors attempt efforts to add some updates and expand their analysis to television, digital media, foreign, and independent films, I did not find their words particularly useful. Deep into the book, there is also some very basic screenwriting advice (formatting, etc.), which seems out of place.

I'm always hesitant to take screenwriting advice from non-professional screenwriters, as these authors are. Even from a film analysis perspective, I was not impressed with their insight here. Although the pursuit of non-traditional scriptwriting is admirable, I would look elsewhere.

title: Good for some but not myself unfortunately (Not recommended for left handed users)
text:
I was a Wacom user for about 12 years, using a Intuos v3 large- Now don't get me wrong, it's not that this tablet is necessarily bad, but I just don't think it's for me. While the drawing surface is about the same size as the intuos 3 I had, the size overall is quite a bit smaller, and I need larger tablets because of my carpal tunnel. I tend to draw with my whole arm/elbow, so it's difficult to adjust to after having a bigger tablet for such a long time.

The surface is also incredibly matte which is... odd feeling? The buttons both on the tablet and the pen are fairly inconveniently placed even for a right handed user I tend to press them often when moving to type or holding the edge as I draw. I can't imagine how bad it'd be for a left handed user. Now to the button on the pen; something about the placement is just... off. I never had this issue with my intuos pen, but I CONSTANTLY press it, which turns the pen off. Constantly. I'll be working and turn off my pen about 4-6 times within about 2 hours maybe?

All in all this tablet just isn't for me and was honestly a quick fix for my previous tablet finally dying on me. I am quite confident at the moment that I'll be going back to wacom once I have the extra income to do so.

Pros:

• The desktop shortcut to the tablet menu is actually quite helpful. It makes it easy to adjust the overall pen pressure of the tablet.
• 8 extra pen nibs in the bottom of the pen stand.

Cons:

• Incredibly matte drawing surface. Which in my personal opinion not as nice as a nice glossy, smooth, drawing surface.
• Shortcut buttons are super inconvenient and poorly placed.
• Button on pen is very poorly placed. Probably one of my biggest issues so far.

title: Observations and reflections exposing the experience of profound loneliness
text: Observation and reflection open the way to understanding.  What's eye opening about this book is how the topic is defined and explored through stories drawn from the real lives of 4 people who experience loneliness in the extreme.  Told as recollections by a lawyer/psychologist, the stories are not dryly analytical, but rather are vivid full color recreations to acquaint us with the full dimensions of a feeling most of us know in small doses.  Why is Facebook popular to the point of obsession?  Does online connectivity somehow nourish a yearning that is growing?  Loneliness is a hot topic, and Freiberg's careful and discerning exposition, which he worked on for several years, isn't trivial, prescriptive or preachy.  As food for thought these accounts are the real deal.  I received the book as a gift, and I'm grateful both to the giver and to the author for enriching my life.

Our cats get very verbal in the wee hours clamoring for us to feed them, so we decided to let them worship a machine instead. title: Limited, superficial, and incomplete (for those who know0
text:
For those who don't know the depth and breadth of Qigong as field of endeavor (not a singular art) with very diverse practices, this is a taste-tester's manual on the topic concerning one of the oldest Qigong systems on record. The problem is ...

(1) it only covers two of the five animals from the ancient sage physician Hua Tou. Which means one's practice is incomplete and out of balance for this particular system.

(2) that no modern scholars are truly certain of how these exercises were conducted, since we have only the sage physician's written descriptions (and not extensive ones) mixed with some cave drawings, and

(3) there are better works that attempt to address not only their own speculations on how these exercises were conducted but also attempt to support such with scholarship and reasoning, drawing on comparative arts inside and outside of the Qigong field, and stepping well beyond mere two sentence sketchy definitions of romanized Chinese terms... as is the case in this book.

If you would like a simple and short manual with direct instructions for soft exercises that might not do enough for you, then maybe this is for you. Or if you're another new ager looking for your next step on a path likely leading nowhere, then this is for you. If you want to explore the range of speculations on this ancient Qigong system, then you might also consider buying it... but only after you've acquired other more comprehensive works on the topic.

title: Grinds well, but fragile
text:
When it's working, it grinds very well and consistently. But it's fragile and I experienced the "lock-up" issue after the first week or so. It is stressful to clean the grinder because I'm always afraid I'll lock it up when trying to reinsert the bean holder.

I gave it four stars because it's an excellent grinder. The fifth star would've been applied if it wasn't so fragile.

Tips to avoid the lock-up issue:

1) Make sure the clear, rubber part of the burr grinder is facing up before you insert the bean holder.
2) Make sure to align the dot on the bean holder as described in the manual.
3) Be sure the bean holder is all the way seated before turning it to engage.
4) Turn it slowly to make sure it's seated and engaging correctly.

Pros:
- Grinds very well and very consistently.
- Good value for the quality of grind.

Cons:
- Very fragile - will lock up occasionally even if you're very careful.
- Lock-up is permanent and requires a replacement grinder.
- Difficult to clean thoroughly - tedious.

title: Better than the movie, but still one of Marvel's weaker '90s efforts.
text:
A decent tale that works better than the Infinity War movie, especially where the character of Thanos is concerned. Even so, this is far from an impressive story arc, and one that becomes muddled and too crammed with characters for its own good. These kind of stories are also difficult to effectively tell when you have a nigh-omnipotent being involved. Marvel still had some great comics in the early '90s like Gruenwald's run on Captain America and Mark Bagley's artistry on Spider-Man, but this book was a sign of things to come as comic plot lines became so mixed up and convoluted that it hurt the industry so badly Marvel nearly went bankrupt.

The best and most effective Marvel superhero crossover is still the original 12-issue Secret Wars series, released in 1984 (and one that had the most lasting consequences, ie Spider-Man's black suit, the Thing leaving the Fantastic Four, etc). Infinity Gauntlet's worth a read, but fails to deliver in its promised scope, and certainly a tale that isn't, by any means, a pivotal moment in Marvel comicdom.

text:
The final book of Lynette Eason's Deadly Reunions triology, When a Secret Kills reveals an ending to this story that no one sees coming.

Jillian Carter finally returns home after 10 years of hiding - running for her life. She's come to the point of no return - the answers must be revealed before anyone else dies. But coming home doesn't solve the problem - only when the truth is revealed will her life and the lives of her friends and family finally be safe again.

Lynette Eason has done a wonderful job of building up a story that keeps readers turning pages, eager to solve the mystery of "who done what" as they cheer on Jillian. From developing characters who are easy to love (or hate in the case of the villains) to keeping readers guessing as they read, Eason has written another stellar novel!

[Spoiler Alert]: One of my favorite aspects of this story is Colton's reaction to meeting his and Jillian's daughter. Even through his anger at missing the first ten years of his little girl's life, the love and acceptance he displays is truly moving.

The characters are sharply drawn both in body and mind, and the plot twists true to both life and character.
Other reviewers are complaining about over-writing. While this may be a bit like grousing that chocolate is rich, Cunningham does stumble here and there, e.g. when he has his hero/narrator say, 'What did Shakespeare say? Our little lives are rounded by a sleep.' This is artificial; Shakespeare himself would have solved the problem by giving that line to the college-student daughter, maybe upon seeing her father drinking vodka in the night!

title: Excellent account of the "Emergency"
text:
I served in the army in Malaya in 1957-58, and found this book to be an excellent "refresher course" when writing my own stories for my family; we have long-standing connections with Malaya, from before WWII until just after Merdeka, and I was able to fill in some gaps and correct some errors.

I've deducted one star because of two problems: first, it is in serious need of an index, and second, there isn't much coverage of the later stages just before Merdeka (August 1957) - perhaps the CTs were effectively beaten by then, but we felt (perhaps mistakenly) that Malaya was still definitely a war zone. I suppose that when you are in the jungle and your rations are being parachuted in you get a distorted view of history!

This book dates from 1971, so naturally does not have some of the information that later writers have been able to find as records are released. I recommend Margaret Shennan's biography of John Davis, "Our Man in Malaya" (2007), as an excellent addition to the field. But of course F. Spencer Chapman's classic, "The Jungle is Neutral", is required reading for anyone trying to understand what jungle warfare really feels like.

title: Warm, enchanting, witty and wise
text: Melanie Rawn is an outstanding writer who intuitively captures the soul of each of her characters and the flavor of their personalities as formed and flawed by experiences within the various shirs, especially the starkness of  The Waste, in which they live and love. She provides colorful and rich  variations on power lust and delicious sexuality that tantalize and reveal.  Exiles and Mageborn Traitor,present a matriarchial society of women as  power brokers and males the home/care givers that challenges the reader to  think about how this could be in "real" life. Her characters are  drawn with insight and thoughtfulness kissed with great wit and wry humor.  She informs the reader of alternate points of view with the graceful  brushstroke of gentle humanity in a smooth, refreshing and thought  provoking way, even when the characters are the villians!  Here is great  mastery in her enchanting style of wrapping you within the cocoon of her  stories where you connect with her characters and what they find funny. The  brilliant description of the arrogant, self absorbed, corpulent,"Grand  Duchess" of Domburr over dressed in gauche yellow riding clothes, with  an orange scarf tied under her chins, heaving her massive bulk onto an even  more massive "plow horse" to go on a hunt is just hilarious. This  dazzling humor is prevalent in her Dragon Prince and Dragon Token series  (which are forerunners in style to this series).  Here we find an even more  powerful fantasy slice of life for those of us addicted to Ms. Rawn's  excellence in writing as her wittiness and sly humor weaves its magical  thread throughout which makes her work so welcome to read.  I look forward  to the blow out mage war between the meleressi and mage guardians in the  forthcoming book Captal's Tower. You can bet Jored and Josselyn will be  nose to toes in that battle!  Will Cailet finds her true love? (Josselyn? )  Will Sarra find someone to ease her broken heart, share her political  battles and warm her lusty nights? Will Teigan's wrenching struggle to open  up to her magic persist after  Glenin's murder of her beloved father?  Will her twin Mikel's magic be supplanted by his evolution into  minstel/bard in Collan/Falundir's place?  Now, to find the clue for that  ornery, sexy, elegant minstrel Collan whose heritage mystery  has  tantalized us throughout this series. I will miss him terribly.

text:
The package comes with two jar openers. I'm still not sure what to do with the second one because my kitchen isn't all that large, so for now I guess I've got a spare. :) I was a little skeptical of the adhesive, because not only does the jar opener need to stick upside down to the bottom of the cabinet, but it also needs to resist the torque of turning the jar every time you use it. Well, so far so good. It's still adhering to my cabinet bottom and it still works.

There are these little metal teeth on one side of the v-shaped recess. You just slide the jar into the recess as far as it will go and turn. The metal teeth grip the lid, so when you turn, you're actually unscrewing the jar from the lid instead of the lid from the jar. And it's really easy. Admittedly, I don't have arthritis in my hands, so I can't say how easy it would be with arthritis. But I am a single woman with limited arm and grip strength. Jars can be a challenge. Opening them with this is safer than banging on the edge of the lid with the handle of a butter knife. And easier, too.

I'd give it 5 stars, but I can't help but wonder about the longevity of the adhesive. Maybe if it's hanging upside down under my cabinet a year from now I'll come back and give it the 5th star. Other composers he knew who were in favor of the regime got fancy "prizes"/gifts of cars, housing, better foods. But he survived  even without those luxuries. I have another compilation of NY Times puzzles that goes back decades which is very challenging because what passed for common knowledge back then is obscure now. However, that's not my issue with Maleska.

With that said, this is the third type of fan I've purchased to replace my defunct one and the only one tall enough and strong enough to work with the height of my bed and layout of my room. title: The Irish Banana Review
text:
Ask the Passengers is exactly the type of book you think you're getting when you read the summary: It's a book about a teenage girl who is trying to sort out her life and figure out who she is and who she wants to be. And yes, it has the added twist of the main character coming to terms with her sexual orientation.

I was a little surprised at how ordinary Astrid felt. Not that I expected her to be some dramatic, overblown character, but I felt like there was nothing spectacular that set her apart from a lot of the other teenage girls I read about in contemporary novels. Her parents don't get her--her mom is more concerned with her sister and her dad is fairly oblivious. That just felt formulaic to me. Aside from the lesbian angle to the story, Astrid felt like any other girl dealing with feelings for that special someone, but unsure of how to express them.

This book is all about emotion. I expected that going in, and A.S. King really does a nice job of expressing those emotions. She phrases things splendidly, and I truly enjoy her writing style. The story flowed nicely. It wasn't overly long or excessively wordy, which could have been an easy pitfall to stumble into.

Overall, this book was exactly what I expected, but that's what disappointed me. I was hoping for something that would wow me. Something I could get really excited about and sink into. The setting is a small town where everyone knows everyone's business, but again, that just felt so done already. I feel like I've read variations of this novel before, but the way King wrote it kept me engaged to the end.

title: Cheap.  Does what I need it to do.  Works with Windows 10.
text:
It's dirt cheap, it connects via bluetooth, and has a built-in trackpad. I use this little keyboard to control my Windows 10 Surface Pro 2 when I have it hooked to the TV for starting up gaming/video sessions (with an Xbox 360 controller taking the USB port) or if I have it hooked to a monitor at the office. While it's not as good a keyboard as the surface pro type cover or some of the fancier/pricier options from Logitech, I'm satisfied given the price.

The keyboard has a built-in battery and charges via USB - one microUSB cable is included if you don't already have one. So far, it seems to hold a charge for a while, as at this point I've only had to charge it once.

If you're packing the keyboard in a bag, make sure to pack it close to something that will give it support, as it's quite thin and would probably flex and get damaged if just carelessly tossed in a bag with a bunch of other stuff.

Some other reviewers said that the keyboard slides around if put on a desk. Mine came with stick-on rubber feet (included in the box) that solved the sliding problem.

Edit: One additional issue I noticed after using it for a while. It doesn't seem that you can disable the "tap to click" feature on the trackpad through Windows 10. This is probably due to the drivers Windows selects for the device, but it still may cause an issue for some potential purchasers who get annoyed with accidentally clicking stuff with their trackpads.

title: Works with Eufy G30 Verge
text: This is the same tape that is included with the Eufy G30 Verge. We purchased a total of 4 rolls of this product to mark off areas in our home. It works when it is exposed on the floor and also when it is under the very edge of thin carpets. We adhered to both the floor and carpet edge, and have not had any issues with lifting. Two important things we have learned: first, all this device needs to sneak through a spot is 4 to 6 inches of gap in the tape. When planning this layout, and you should plan it before you cut it, make sure you are not leaving any gaps in the tape. Secondly, if you are concerned about damaging your floor with the 3M double-sided tape that is enclosed, we used 3M command strips with a 3-pound weight classification. We were able to purchase a package of these separate of command hooks they are typically used with. Since we have hardwood floors, we thought this was a worthy investment. All tape was mounted with the light side facing upward. The device has not crossed any of the magnetic barriers including thresholds. I should add that we do not have any metal threshold in our home, it is all wood, tile, carpet, and vinyl. The tape is an investment that can be costly but it is absolutely worth it. We returned a similar product because it did not work but this barrier tape has performed 100%. It also has a lower profile then other barrier tape we tried so it lays nice and flat under area rugs and in high traffic areas. Highly recommend.

title: More informative than grouchy!
text:
"The Grouchy Grammarian" is not a grouchy book. Parrish's fictional curmudgeon limits his irritation to public figures and national media outlets for spreading grammatical errors and "infelicities" throughout the populace. Parrish constructively channels his alter-ego's concerns, and the result is enlightening rather than chastening. Among usage guides, this one is particularly helpful for three reasons:
1) Each topic is covered in a short chapter, and each chapter ends with a summary so you can learn a lot quickly.
2) Parrish includes a thorough index, and a thoughtful annotated bibliography of guides to language, writing and usage.
3) Parrish clearly explains why usage glitches are glitches. Now that I understand what NOT to do, I don't have to laboriously memorize rules about what to do. Rote memorization of grammar rules never worked for me--I resemble the student in "Up the Down Staircase" who complains that "semicolons don't stick to my head."
I wish all people who worry about "weak", "watery" assaults upon English had mediators like Parrish to absorb their ire and deftly convey their championship and knowledge of precise language.

title: Gritty and grim yet inexplicably hopeful
text:
Sabaal is a captive Jakkattu imprisoned on Earth by the Mezna priests who experiment on her. Javan 6ix is a tek - half Miscegenate, half machine - beginning to question his life in the city. Norwood Thorne is too smart for a human, too inquisitive for a man, leading his sister Julip down the path of questioning the Temple, the Mezna and all the history they've learnt on the Rez.

Sabaal's escape is the part of the catalyst that throws them all together, leading them to question whether everything the Mezna has been telling them is true. Because beyond their fences, the Feral - the Undone as they name themselves - have information that will turn their understanding of the world upside down.

The Jakkattu Vector is action-packed, with Tyler propelling you from one scene to another, giving you glimpses of the truth, glimmers of the lies these human-Mezna hybrids have grown up with, expecting you to piece them all together before the horrifying reveal. In between, she engages your emotions with the innocence of the young Thornes as they grow up, navigating the thin line between independence and insolence in their quest for truth. And then she feeds you heartbreak on a platter.

The Jakkattu Vector is gritty and grim yet inexplicably hopeful as each of strand of humanity - human, Miscegenate, Undone - come to terms with who they are and what the Mezna has done to them.

title: CV195 Battery Compartment Mysteries!
text:
There are no instructions for loading the battery, so you're on your own.

My attempt began with pushing-in on the little button on the one muff. It looks like you would push in on the button, and then pull-up on the oval plastic disk just above the button. But nooooo!

Push down on that button, and at the same time SLIDE the plastic shroud below there downward a little. It's on a hinge, so don't make the mistake of yanking it off!

Rotate the shroud up and out of the way to install the battery. The flat side of the battery goes in first, with the positive terminal facing out as you push it in there. With mine, the battery supplied was dead, so I tried another and it works fine. No issues with the battery not fitting. Fits well.

I wonder how many customers will try it with the supplied "dead" battery, assume the headphones are defective, and return the unit immediately? Probably many will. It DID cross my mind. Good thing I had a few AAA batteries around here.

A few words of instructions to install the battery would be helpful. Might save them some expense for returned items, too, making it extremely cost effective. Doh!

title: I cannot express fully how much I enjoyed Durga Chew-Bose's collection of essays
text:
I cannot express fully how much I enjoyed Durga Chew-Bose's collection of essays. I felt drunk on this book. I rarely underline or write in books, but I couldn't help myself with this one: Chew-Bose's writing is so unique, yet so relatable at the same time. She put to words feelings I've had—of being young, of being a woman, of the relationship you have with your parents—that I've never expressed, feelings and thoughts I didn't realize others shared too, that I now realize are possibly universal parts of growing up. I read, reread, wrote down passages, sighed after reading many more. I savored this book.

"Your hot friend on a balmy summer night telling you about some good news in her life is—how do I put this without sounding absurd? It's barometric. It's love and you love's power growing, and it's watching the elements cater to a woman who exudes."

"We are waking up to freckles dotting a person's back, and leveling that we might be in love—not with this person, but with freckles and downy morning light, because unfamiliar contours before 9 a.m. have a way. With someone new, even freckles become spotless. They are a surface blurred and time deferred. Everything begins simply enough."

I texted excerpts to friends, including the two above, and three asked to borrow it. Of course, I need to reread it a third time before I lend it out (I may just purchase a second copy). This book is a marvel—I can't wait to read what Chew-Bose writes next.

text:
This is the 7th DHMD-210 (or replacement model) we have received in the

Despite this high failure rate, I still think this is a great little
product for the price. We keep one in our 24' travel trailer, two in my
wife's weaving studios and one in our downstairs family room. The ones
in the family room and in one of the weaving studios are clearly being
pushed beyond their advertised limits for room size, but they pull a lot
of moisture out of the air and we don't want to invest in larger units
for those two spaces so we continue using them and just remember to
empty them frequently. The unit that is in our trailer is unheated and
will occasionally freeze up during the winter; it continues to run but
the vents get covered in ice so no more moisture collects in the water
tank. But we bring it into the house and, after the ice thaws, the unit
resumes normal operation. We'll continue to use this product and
replace them as needed, but now I spend the extra $1 or 2 for the
extended warranty (which I haven't had to use yet). Overall, I would
rate this product as a 4 on a scale of 1-5, 5 being the highest. The
only reason I don't give it a 5 is the high failure rate and not being
able to figure out whether the failure is in the unit itself or in the
power supply so that the entire unit doesn't need to be thrown away when
one fails.

title: Just one question:  Why?
text:
In five editions (and counting of the Physical Basis for the Direction of Time) Dieter Zee has been asking the same question: What laws of the universe are actually law like and what laws of the universe are merely fact like?

This is a question very much at the heart of this brief accessible tome wherein Great Britain's Royal Astronomer probes the significance of two microscopic numbers and four macroscopic numbers that seem to effect the raison d'etre of the universe.

Along the way we deal with claims such as the cosmic anthropologic hypothesis which assert that the universe was created specifically the way it was in order to allow life (an assertion a little like Goldfish saying that the aquarium in which they live and the country house that supports it was created specifically for them).

Things happen and unless you're Paul Davies and writing any of his major works on the matter (starting with God and the New Physics proceeding to the award winning Mind of God and finally concluding with the hard back title Cosmic Jackpot) we are merely "a thing that happened."

Humbling no doubt but a likely consequence of fraction of a fraction of fraction of...you get the point...of our occupying the merest miniscule part of creation.

But this book is important reading. Like any good reporting it lays out the conventional wisdom (of 1999, still sadly all too current in 2009) and leaves the reader to decide.

Why? In it's ultimate sense the question will always remain a personal one. But at least science can say, and purport to actually prove, that we're in there somewhere.

title: Wonderful Book - Looking forward to a 2nd Ed.
text:
Fr. Emmanuel does an admirable job of commenting on various liturgical questions, and does not balk at some of the more contentious issues (cf. "The Gate and the Curtain" pp. 181-2; who knew that St. John Chrysostom mentioned the use of a Curtain?!), providing multiple perspectives. It is set up as a textbook including multiple layers of depth in commentary, from the more casual student of Liturgy, to the more scholarly.

A second edition would be most welcome, as there are a number of page cross-references which are incorrect, and at least one diagram is mentioned which does not appear in the text. Much recourse in footnotes is made to electronic sources, which may simply be the direction of modern scholarship, but does evoke a double-take when used in a field that stretches back millennia.

In all, a wonderful start, and a second edition to take care of minor housekeeping issues will be most enthusiastically received.

title: Great customer service added two stars!
text:
UPDATE:

I have added two stars to this drone review. The customer service from Dynalog is outstanding. Katelin from Dynalog reached out to me after my initial review to see if they could help resolve my issues with the drone. Several days passed with back and forth emails...and then bingo! They got the app working with my phone. At the time I am writing this update, downloading the app using the QR code failed for me. However, you search the app store for Dynalog Casper and download the app there, you hopefully will have the same success as I did. After connecting my phone to the drone's wifi and starting the app, I had video from the drone. I was able to record video and take photos. After playing with this drone, I can say that it is a great starter drone to get your feet wet in the world of flying drones. I can now definitely recommend this as a great starter drone for anyone.

Original review below:

This is really a neat little drone. It is amazing all of the features that this tiny little drone has. It comes with two batteries to keep you flying longer and even two usb chargers for each battery. Included is another full set of propellers and screws. The remote has nice one-touch built in functions. It all around the drone is fun to play with.

However, here is the deal breaker. The app is not supported by my phone. I have a Samsung S21 5G phone. When I scanned the QR code in the quick start manual, the APP indicates that it is not compatible with my phone. Another reviewer has mentioned that their phone was not compatible with the app either. The point of having a drone is to view and record video from the flight. Without this feature, there is no point in owning the drone.

The hardware is great, but the software evidentially is still in the development stage. Keep shopping. You will be disappointed in this one. I will change my review should software for this drone ever be developed for a larger base of phones.

title: Unimpressed
text:
This looks like a fun puzzle. The concept is great. The execution? Not so much.

First of all, this puzzle, which is the size of two old 45 records stacked atop one another, arrives in a plastic package the size of your house.

Well, maybe not quite that big, but it is much, much larger than necessary. MUCH larger. So I was already not very happy with it. Then, I tried to open it, and made another discovery: if you for some reason need to perform emergency surgery in your home, the plastic encasing this puzzle will double as a scalpel.

Honestly, I think they just want you to buy it and put it on display in the box. This package is next to impossible to open.

And wasteful. Did I mention yet that this plastic package is much, much too big for it’s contents? Because it is.

Once I finally got the puzzle out, I mixed it up, spun it round, did the entire hokey-pokey. Then I started the process of solving it. I ordered the most challenging one since I am good at puzzles and wanted something that would tax my brain.

I am little, and have the hands to match. Even my childlike fingers had difficulty maneuvering the tiny inner rings. After about the fifth one from the center, it gets easier.

It took me under three minutes to solve. For the most difficult one. Counting the issues I had moving and turning the tiniest rings. Either I am some sort of prodigy, or this doesn’t deliver on the hours of fun puzzling promised. I tried the other side to see if it was a fluke. It was not. Nor is this like a Rubik’s Cube, where after you solve it, it’s fun to mix it up and try again. I haven’t had the urge to pick it up again after my initial tests, which I think says something.

Bottom line: extremely wasteful packaging containing a no-challenge “puzzle.” Maybe this would be better marketed as a fidget toy. Or to very small children. Would not recommend.

title: Highly entertaining!
text:
Jim Swain’s novels have entertained me for years…especially his Tony Valentine series.

In “Take Down,” Jim returns to the world of the gambling/casino scams and it’s big fun.

Billy Cunningham is a captivating casino scam artist…who truly puts the art in casino scam artist.

He’s a raconteur, a rascal, well prepared and always has a Plan B.

Billy has had a successful career in Las Vegas, and the gaming commission will stop at nothing to put him away.

No matter, Billy has planned an intricate scheme to relieve a casino of $8,000,000.00. His crew has all the right pieces and the game’s afoot.

The plot moves rapidly and any impediment that could arise…does. As the obstacles appear, Billy’s brilliant criminal mind finds a work-around.

Billy lives by the “honor among thieves” code, and that noble quality is tested on many occasions as the gaming commission attempts to squeeze him.

There are numerous capers within the caper. The characters, infamous and otherwise are colorful and eclectic. Jim tells a great tale, as usual.

In the final pages, there are signs that there will be more to come for Billy and his crew. That’s great news!

He's small enough to fit in your pocket so you can stroll around Cybertron with him to keep those other sectors in line. War for Cybertron reference aside....

PARENTS: This is an awesome little toy for young and adult Transformers fans. Shockwave is this character's name and he is one of the primary villains (Decepticon team) in the Transformer shows. He's basically 2nd in command to Megatron (the chief villain/antagonist). This Shockwave model is only 13 steps to transform, which may prove difficult for young children who are inexperienced with Transformer toys. For those children, I'd recommend the 1-step line of toys (Cybertron Adventures and Rescue Bots). My 4 year old has a lot of exposure to my complex Transformer collection, so he powers through 13 steps without a sweat. Note that the hand cannon is detachable, so be wary of losing this to the couch cushion abyss like the rest of your kid's toy accessories. Lastly, this is a "core class" figure, so it's relatively small at 3.5" when standing in robot mode.

My opinion of this model is very positive. For such a small scale, the sculpting work is super detailed and it does a near perfect job of capturing Shockwave's "Gen1" appearance (except for the angry brow). His robot-mode transformation is engineered well, tight joints/pivots and no fear of breaking any brittle pieces. The alt-mode (a tank?) is acceptable, but I've no major complaints about either mode.

text: This cage is bigger than I thought, and is perfect for my indian ringneck parakeet! She loves it! I would not put a bird with feet smaller than an indian ringneck's in this cage,  as a smaller bird will not be able to climb the walls in this cage. King's cages are well-known for being top-of-the-line and well-built, and this cage lives up to that expectation.  I purchased the white version that has the 5/8" bar spacing (it is also available with 1" bar spacing), it arrived by frieght delivery in pieces in two boxes on a pallet and was very well-packed, so I was able to pre-schedule the delivery date. It came with vague assembly instructions, but was fairly easy to put together. I was able to assemble the entire cage by myself, which was an accomplishment for a 5-foot tall woman! It has very sturdy casters that screw into steel and they move very smoothly.  The perches are HUGE (basically for a cockatoo or double-yellowhead amazon size bird), so I purchased 3/4" unsealed/untreated pine dowels at Home Depot, cut them to the lengths I needed and notched them. One engineering issue I found with this cage is that the placement of the door is too far to the right, which makes it impossible to run a perch all the way across the cage in front of the food and water dishes. King's could have avoided this problem by just shifting the door about 2-inches to the left. I solved this problem using PVC pipe and fittings from the plumbing section of a home improvement store. The locks on this cage are bird-proof.  I love this cage! It is beautiful, sturdy, very well-made, roomy, and has a built-in play stand. My bird loves it, too!

title: Sebastian has been trapped inside a dark dimension, and the three horsemen will do anything
text:
The final book of the Riders duology, and I’m happy with how it ended. Seeker by Veronica Rossi picks up where Riders left off. Sebastian has been trapped inside a dark dimension, and Darryn and the remaining three horsemen will do anything to bring him back.

One thing that I don’t care for about this book is the romance. Not every story needs a love story, especially a story that’s so tightly focused on a group of friends. The romance didn’t add to the story and Darryn’s continuous pulling away from Gideon was exasperating by the middle of the book.

Cutting the romance out of the story, like Riders, it’s a very neat story with a unique point of view. The remaining horsemen are doing all they can to find Bass in The Rift. The Rift forces them to face their fears, and face their innermost demons.

Without giving much away, the journey to find Sebastian is one full of haunting memories and really learning more about the characters. I don’t feel like there was as much character development as their was in the previous book, but I don’t think that it’s really a bad thing with this book. I also wish that this book only had Darryn’s or only Gideon’s point of view, like the first book, and not bouncing between both.

I do wish there were more books in the series. Books from the other horsemen’s points of views would be interesting, and I’d definitely read them. All in all, a series that is enjoyable and provides a pretty unique premise for the characters.

title: A Funny Man Revealed
text:
I remember watching Steve Martin's seemingly meteoric rise from Tonight Show guest, to Saturday Night Live stalwart, to concert hall blockbuster. He made me laugh. He helped take the edge off the 70's. I remember leaving one of his Nassau Coliseum shows thinking that all in the world was good and it's ok to be goofy - for a little while anyway. It was from that melancholy recollection I read through this book.

While Martin's stand up humor was edgy, innovative, and visual, Born Standing Up is laced with a dry humor that sometimes brings chuckles one or two lines afterward. We can see that as is true for most seemingly overnight success stories there are years of hard work and sacrifice behind the sensation. Though there is only a small window into Steve's creative genius, you can see how his young life contributed to the product he presented on stage. Martin's stand up act was filled with silliness, idiocy, and just plain tomfoolery. In Born Standing Up we see the crafting of that act took an intellectual approach and technical dissection of how comedy works. Laced with stories of his family life, upstart employment, inspirations, encounters and collaborations with familiar performers from the era, and the eventual eruption of his show, Born Standing Up leads down a road of opportunities realized and acted upon.

Tracking the career of Steve Martin can be confusing. The performances of the stand up era are dramatically different from the ones we see in movies today. So different that when I played some of "Let's Get Small" for my kids (who are very familiar with the Cheaper by the Dozen dad) they had a hard time believing it is the same person. Born Standing Up reveals an underlying personality that is constant throughout Martin's career.

I believe this is a 5 star book for anyone who fondly remembers Martin's stand-up. Thanks Steve for making the world a little less serious!

This book contains several different stories, totally unrelated. OK, so they each mention somebody in one of the other stories, but that's a big stretch to make them connected. I kept expecting them to come together at the end, but alas, you never find out what happened to the snottie after her first cruise, except that she became famous. The cats' plans are spelled out, but then what ever happened to them? (Not even an oblique reference later on.) A kidnapped girl has almost nothing to do with the confusing political intrigue that she shares a quarter of the pages with. And a battle shapes up for control of a government, only to be wrapped up abruptly in one page.
The stories don't stand on their own and they don't fit together between the covers of one book. Only read it if you have already read other books by the author and want to see some scraps from the cutting room floor.

title: Tiny charger with very detailed information in the product description
text: This product came with the single battery charger and 19" USB-A to micro-USB cable.  There's no manual included but all the information is on the product listing and description.  For about $6, this good deal if you wanted a compact single cell charger.  It's rated at 1A charging.  So, it's a fast charger compared to the normally 300 mA or 500 mA chargers.  The 18650 battery I'm charging does get warm when charging but that's normal for fast chargers.  Though it could mean it would not help extend the life of the battery.  Please note that this charger was designed only for Li-ON batteries of a certain size.  Don't try charging Ni-MH, Ni-Cd, AA, AAA, AAAA, nor C batteries.  They are normally 1.2 V batteries and will more than likely get damaged by charging at 4.2v 1A.  It's a compact design built for portability.  I don't see the sense in complaining about the micro-USB end of the cable because it goes right into the charger base.  And the USB-A end would fit in any USB 2.0 or USB 3.0 port or wall adapter. title: An amazing emotional roller-coaster of a story.
text:
POSSIBLE SPOILERS AHEAD:

I honestly have to say that it's not only the best book I've ever read but probably one of the greatest pieces of writing I've ever read. From beginning to end, I found myself completely drawn to the story of Jersey City bus driver Andre Bolden.

The book is a real page turner and what really kept me hooked besides wanting to know the story resolution was the relationship between Andre and Sandra, the mother of his son. Sandra had so much resistance towards him that I kept turning pages eager to see if Andre could ever get over that emotional fortress. At the same time, the theme about snitching itself was handled very well by Mr. Mattison without being too imposing about it. Rather than making it about a guy or people around him who don't snitch, it comes across as a story of a man whose wrong choices in life start to eat him up bit by bit, living in the fear of losing his life as he had with getting kicked out of school, losing Sandra, and eventually losing his job. He thinks living back with Sandra and Little Dre would solve all his problems. But what transpires over the course of the book leads Andre to a much higher purpose of standing up for himself and those dearest to him.

I also want to applaud Mr. Mattison himself for being able to write the book using little to no profanity. I'm sure it was quite a challenge to do that given the genre and the tone of the book.

Overall, this is a must read for teenagers and adults across America. Look forward to the movie adaptation.

As the host of The Wired Educator Podcast and the Director of Innovation and Instruction for Port Clinton Schools, it has always been my primary mission to celebrate and promote the voices of outstanding educators. Congratulations Keven on an amazing book and making a global impact on education. Well done.
Kelly Croy

title: A Very Good Electric Shaver for Sensitive Skin
text:
As someone with very sensitive skin, I have always had problems with razor burn after shaving. Dry electric shavers tend to butcher my skin. Traditional multi-blade razors (like the Mach 3) are easier on my skin, but as sensitive as my skin is, cuts are not uncommon. A few months ago I received a Norelco 7735X Cool Skin Additive In/Out of Shower Shaver as a gift and gave it a try. Thanks to the shaving gel that can be applied to the skin at the touch of a button while shaving, it provides a very close shave that doesn't cut my skin like a traditional razor, and there's very little skin irritation afterwards. As for closeness, I'd say that it's almost as good as a Mach 3 razor.

One aspect about this shaver that I like is that it operates from a rechargeable battery so that there's no electric cord to get in the way while shaving. Also, the shaving gel packets are easy to replace, it comes with a charger stand, it's easy to clean the rotating blades and it takes up little bathroom counter space. Further, it takes less time to shave and clean-up afterwards than with a traditional razor & shaving cream.

Overall, I regard the Norelco 7735X Cool Skin Additive In/Out of Shower Shaver as a very good shaver and rate it with 5 out of 5 stars. Granted, it is somewhat expensive, but if you have very sensitive skin like me, you might be as pleasantly surprised as I was with its performance.

This is an excellent choice if you are trying to drink 8 glasses of water a day. You can take 8 glasses, pour it in all at once, pour the 8 glasses into your container or hydration pack of choice and off you go. Simplicity itself. The pitcher holds at least 16 glasses, so someone else in the family can get their 8 glasses too. I was well hydrated when using this pitcher. CONS: Children 3 - 8 can not handle this pitcher at all. When they try to use the spigot, they tip the whole pitcher accidentally on the floor and it shatters. I did try the metal version of this pitcher, but still fell and still shattered at the plastic. It doesn't have that always pour lid, so they pour it when it is still filtering and water pours every where. They drop and break it before the filter wears out.

I also tried pouring the filtered water in a metal pitcher for them (preferring to avoid plastic) but since it was metal, it was hard to monitor when they'd need a refill so that didn't work great. I did also try a plastic pitcher for them, which they still dropped and broke and that could be an OK solution because it is a lot cheaper to replace a simple plastic pitcher than this expensive filtration pitcher.

Finally, they did well with the Zero Water 8 glass round pitcher. Never dropped it once. But you can only put about 3 glasses of water at a time and it is like a 30 minute project to get your 8 glasses filtered. My water consumption honestly went down using that product. But it was the only sensible option. I know they have a glass 40 cup stand. But I just have nightmares of glass and gallons of water on the floor and couldn't bring myself to buy it.

The kids are older, and I really need to drink 8 glasses per day so I'm try this again. Should they break it AGAIN, the round pitcher will be the kids pitcher and this one be off limits to them.

title: Better respected than loved.
text:
"The Morels", a debut novel by Christopher Hacker, is one of those novels that can be described as better respected than loved. The story - a story within a story - is the tale of how a bunch of bad decisions have affected the lives of at least three generations of one family - the Morels - and those of people tangentially connected with them.

Arthur Morel, a musical prodigy, only child of divorced parents has walked through life in seeming non-connection with the realities we all have to deal with. After a particularly beautiful musical recital, the teenaged Arthur has performed an on-stage act of defilement that has stunned and revolted his audience. The years pass, Arthur has met, married a young woman called Penelope, and fathered a son, Will, with her. Penelope supports the family as a pastry chef while Arthur continues to "dabble" with life. He publishes a well-received novel and is in the process of finishing his second novel, called "The Morels", when Christopher Hacker's book begins. The story Hacker tells is narrated by a young man - himself adrift in movie making - who had known Arthur as the young defiler and now moves back into Arthur's life. He acts as teller of Arthur's story and its major interpreter.

"Interpreted" because there are a lot of actions which need to be interpreted to both those affected by the actions and those merely standing-by, observing. Are a man's possible incestuous thoughts always acted on - or can they merely remain, safely, thoughts? Where do lies and truth-telling become hopelessly meshed until neither is recognisable? In a broad way, Hacker's book is a bit like "The Dinner", by Herman Koch, another book where families and lies are tossed together and the truth never quite emerges.

Christopher Hacker's book should make the reader think about truth and lies and that muddy middle in between. Arthur, Penelope, and Will Morel are victims of both lies and truth, which they, themselves, perpetrate. It's an interesting book.

She has an independent and feisty heroine in Madeline (Maddie) Fitzgerald, a determined and sexy hero in Sam McCabe and lots of fun secondary characters such as E.P. Wynee, Sam's partner; Cynthia Gardner, also on Sam's team and Jon and Susan. The dog, Zelda, is also a riot.

McCabe is an FBI special agent tracking a serial killer who calls him to leave clues. Maddie is the proud owner of a small advertising agency that is due to make a presentation the next morning at a dog food manufacturing company in New Orleans. Maddie is attacked and nearly killed in her hotel room. The killer also kills another Madeline Fitzgerald who is staying at the same hotel that same night/early morning. Maddie has secrets in her past that make her distrust law enforcement in general and the FBI in particular so lots of fireworks when McCabe & Wynne track her down to question her. Maddie & Jon make their presentation and win business with the dog food company by suggesting the owner's dog to appear in the ads and on a new logo.

Maddie & Jon fly back to St. Louis but Maddie is afraid her past is catching up with her. In the meantime, McCabe is convinced the killer will go after her again as she is the one who got away. Lots of close calls, comic relief from Zelda (the dog) and Wynne, romance and plots twists follow.

A delightful and thrilling read if you like mystery, thrills and some humor!
