title: Eh, its ok
text: This is kinda a weird item.  Neat idea, but weird.  I have extended magazines that came with my Sig pistol and they fit okay.  The problem with extended mags is they don't fit in most mag holders because they are overly tall and the flap doesn't velcro shut like it should.  The flaps on this pouch grab the velcro with my mags inside, but just barely.  You can fold the flaps back entirely and use the "griptite" feature to hold the magazines.  I keep going back and forth on whether I like the "griptite" design.  It consists of plastic clips that grab the magazines, which fold into the cordura material in a pocket.  Hard to explain, but when you put your mag in the plastic acts as a spring and squeezes your magazine.  The mag slides out with a mild tug.  They make the overall pouch much thicker, probably twice as thick as the magazine would be otherwise.  I think I would prefer a simple pouch over a gee-whiz clippy thing.  I suspect these would be great if you knew you would be standing up while using them (such as on the range or at a match).  If you were crawling around in the dirt with these they still might fall out (even with the "griptite" feature) and your magazines would certainly get dirty.  These are not great for keeping your mags out of the elements.  But i suppose it's a trade off.  They are quite speedy to get out and would make for quick mag changes.  They're cheap enough- try them out for yourself!

title: Not my favorite Meg Cabot book
text:
I read this book last Summer and I wasn't in love with it. I've loved all of the other books Meg Cabot has written for adults but I didn't really care for Lizzie. Which was a problem for me since the book is written in the first person. The whole ditzy-whoops I opened my big mouth again thing got old. I definitely enjoy Meg's other series of Heather Wells and the "Boy" series (you know, the ones that are set in e-mail format) more.

The story of Lizzie going to England to be with her thought to be love of her life was okay. That had a few humorous moments. The story that takes in Southern France was alright too but very predictable.

So the plot was predictable but okay but the character of Lizzie made it difficult to really enjoy it. But that being said, I will probably read the second book when it comes in paperback to see if it's better than the first book.

title: Love it.
text: I love this hair. I was debating whether to write a review as the seller my decide to up the price and I hope they dont but I really love this hair.  I am sorry I probably should have taken few pics to post to show the different ways I wear this hair.  When I was considering to buy this hair the first time and I read the reviews, I saw where people mentioned using 2 packs of hair so I bought 4 packs.  My first time I used 1 pack and i think 1/2 of one bundle from the second pack. With my second install I used a little less and for my third install I used less than 1 pack.  I have had the hair in for about a month with the last install and it is still going.  I did learn a few tricks as although the hair is light, it tangles and knots easily however, I will not be selfish and share my hacks.  To keep the curls longer, after you have installed the hair go over the hair with Shine n Jam. Take the time and do small sections, it will be worth it. My first install I didn't add any products and then it started matting after a few days and then when I tried to add products it was matted and heavy.  With my second install I used Eco styler gel which did lessen the matting for a little but the hair was flaky.  On the last install I used the shine n jam as soon as I finished the install. I have no flakes, the hair is still cute after a month. I do trim the ends as it will knot.  I just bought another 4 packs. Again I hope they dont increase the price but for $20 I can get 3 or 4 hair styles which is a bargain. My only downside was the color. I usually buy 2 but their 2 is lighter than my hair. Not very noticeable unless you are hung up like me. I love the hair.
